viral_video_prompts.text:
- APPLE:
First-person POV starting in a bright supermarket aisle. Realistic human hands reach forward and grasp a fresh apple from the display, then slowly bring it closer to the camera. As the apple enters focus, layered holographic AR interface elements fade in and materialize around the fruit—nutrition data panels, calorie count, animated vitamin icons that pulse softly, a freshness score that increments upward, and recipe cards that slide into view from the sides.
The UI elements continuously float and subtly reorganize themselves, following the natural micro-movements of the hand holding the apple, as if reacting dynamically to the user’s shifting gaze and attention. Individual data panels gently bob and tilt in 3D space. On the left peripheral vision, a vertical translucent shopping list HUD remains anchored, with items checking themselves off with smooth animations and green checkmarks appearing.
The camera occasionally shifts focus between the apple in hand and the AR interface elements, creating natural depth-of-field transitions. Ambient light reflects realistically off the holographic glass-like UI panels, casting soft glows. The hand subtly rotates the apple, causing the AR overlays to reposition and track the fruit’s orientation in real-time.
Hyper-realistic mixed reality aesthetic, clean futuristic AR design, smooth UI animations, glass-like translucent panels, soft ambient glow, realistic lighting and shadows, natural depth of field shifts, immersive first-person interface, next-generation retail experience.

- Vase
First-person POV standing in a softly lit art gallery. Realistic human hands reach forward and gently lift a small ancient artifact (ceramic vase) from a pedestal display. As the object comes closer to the camera, layered holographic AR interface elements fade in around it—historical timeline, origin map that zooms from satellite view to excavation site, 3D cross-section showing internal structure, authenticated provenance chain, and related artifact thumbnails that slide into view.
The UI elements continuously float and subtly reorganize themselves, following the natural rotation of the hands turning the vase, as if reacting dynamically to the user’s shifting gaze. Individual data panels gently bob and tilt in 3D space. On the left peripheral vision, a vertical translucent tour guide HUD remains anchored, with exhibition points checking themselves off with smooth animations.
The camera occasionally shifts focus between the artifact’s surface details and the AR interface elements, creating natural depth-of-field transitions. Ambient gallery light reflects realistically off the holographic glass-like UI panels. The hands subtly rotate the vase, causing AR overlays to highlight different decorative patterns and timestamp markers in real-time.
Hyper-realistic mixed reality aesthetic, clean futuristic AR design, smooth UI animations, glass-like translucent panels, soft ambient glow, museum lighting, natural depth of field shifts, immersive first-person interface, next-generation cultural experience. Duration: 5-10 seconds.

- Plant:
First-person POV standing in a bright home interior near a window. Realistic human hands reach forward and cradle a potted houseplant (monstera deliciosa), bringing it closer to the camera. As the plant enters focus, layered holographic AR interface elements materialize around the leaves—soil moisture level with animated water droplets, sunlight exposure heatmap, growth progress timeline, watering schedule reminders, and care tip cards that slide into view.
The UI elements continuously float and respond to the plant’s swaying leaves, reorganizing themselves as if reacting to the user’s attention on specific leaves or stems. On the right peripheral vision, a vertical translucent smart home HUD displays other plants’ status indicators with animated icons.
The camera shifts focus between the detailed leaf texture and the AR data layers. Natural window light creates realistic reflections on the holographic panels. The hands gently turn the pot, causing AR overlays to track and analyze different parts of the plant in real-time.
Hyper-realistic mixed reality aesthetic, organic botanical interface design, smooth UI animations, glass-like panels, natural lighting, depth of field shifts, immersive smart home experience. Duration: 5-10 seconds.

- Pills:
First-person POV standing at a modern pharmacy counter. Realistic human hands pick up a medication bottle and bring it close to the camera. Layered holographic AR interface elements appear around the bottle—active ingredient breakdown with molecular structures, dosage instructions with animated pill icons, potential drug interaction warnings, patient reviews rated by helpfulness, and pharmacy location map for refills.
The UI elements float and reorganize based on which label section the gaze focuses on. On the left peripheral vision, a vertical translucent health profile HUD shows current medications and allergy alerts with gentle pulse animations.
The camera shifts focus between the prescription label and floating AR data. Clinical lighting reflects off the holographic panels. The hands rotate the bottle, triggering different information layers to highlight and expand in real-time.
Hyper-realistic mixed reality aesthetic, clean medical interface design, smooth animations, glass-like panels, clinical lighting, next-generation healthcare experience. Duration: 5-10 seconds.

## Overview
This guide demonstrates how to create a seamless morphing video sequence using AI image generation followed by image-to-video animation. The final result transforms a man cutting a tomato into a futuristic architectural structure.

## Step 1: Generate All Frame Images

## Image 1 – Opening Scene

A medium close-up of a man. He holds a shiny silver kitchen knife in his right hand raised above, and a ripe red tomato in his left hand below. The background is solid black. He looks directly at the camera with a focused, intense expression. Studio lighting.
- -

## Image 2 – Isolated Tomato
Purpose: Transition focus to the tomato alone
Reference: Use Image 1 as reference
Prompt:
A single, perfect red tomato sitting on a dark surface. Pitch black background, cinematic rim lighting, sharp focus, hyper-realistic product photography.

## Image 3 – Exploded Diagram

A 3D scientific illustration of a tomato exploded into vertical floating layers (skin, flesh, seeds). Dark background, white text labels with leader lines pointing to specific parts, digital art style.
- -

## Image 4 – Cross-Section
Purpose: Reveal internal tomato structure
Reference: Use Image 2 as reference
Prompt:
The same tomato now split into two perfect halves on a dark surface, showing the internal cross-section with visible seeds, pulp, and chambers. The cut is clean and symmetrical. Moody, dark studio lighting with reflections on the wet interior surfaces.
- -

## Image 5 – Architectural Finale
Purpose: Final transformation into architecture
Reference: Use Image 4 as reference
Prompt:
A futuristic architectural building at night, organic curved shape resembling a sliced tomato cross-section. Glowing red interior lighting, glass facade with intricate structural web, street level view with people walking on the sidewalk. Hyper-realistic, 8k resolution, cinematic atmosphere, parametric design style.

## Step 2: Generate Video Sequences

## Video 1: Man to Tomato Transition
First Frame: Image 1
Last Frame: Image 2
Motion Prompt: The man places the tomato on the table
Transition Purpose: Human subject exits, focus shifts to object

## Video 2: Tomato Explosion
First Frame: Image 2
Last Frame: Image 3
Motion Prompt: A tomato fully exploded into floating horizontal slices in a dark void, layers spread far apart. Scientific 3D rendering with glowing text labels clearly visible
Transition Purpose: Whole object transforms into exploded diagram

## Video 3: Diagram to Cross-Section
First Frame: Image 3
Last Frame: Image 4
Motion Prompt: The floating tomato layers collapse back together, reassembling into the split cross-section view on the dark surface
Transition Purpose: Diagram reassembles into cut tomato

## Video 4: Tomato to Architecture
First Frame: Image 4
Last Frame: Image 5
Motion Prompt: A close-up cross-section of a red tomato morphing into a futuristic, red-tinted architectural building. The tomato pulp turns into glass windows and curved structural beams. Cinematic night shot, street level view with people walking, hyper-realistic architectural visualization
Transition Purpose: Organic form morphs into architectural structure

## Pro Tips
- Maintain Consistency: Always use reference images to ensure visual continuity between frames

- Lighting Coherence: Keep the dark/moody lighting theme consistent throughout all images

- Color Palette: The red tomato color should thread through to the red-lit architecture

- Timing: Adjust video sequence duration based on your chosen AI video tool’s capabilities

A rain-soaked underground tavern at midnight. Lanterns flicker, puddles on stone floors reflect amber light. A lone man stands at the center — sharp jawline, dark eyes, calm expression, wearing a deep crimson longcoat over black, a silver chain at his neck. He holds a sleek blade at his side, perfectly still.
Camera descends slowly from bird’s-eye. Cut to tight side-profile close-up — rain slides down his face as he slowly lifts his eyes with cold, lethal precision.
The room explodes. Eight masked operatives in black flood in from the rooftop hatch, stairwell, and rear entrance simultaneously. Low-angle shot captures them dropping mid-leap, blades drawn — steel rings against the sound of heavy rain.
He steps onto a table and launches upward. Slow-motion: he vaults between tables, flipping one with a single arm to slam two attackers. Fast cuts to close-up combat — spinning, blocking, countering in one fluid motion. One pivot — two men down. His blade slices the rain into curving arcs of water.
Camera whips laterally as the fight peaks — side kick, wide sword sweep, flying strikes off table edges. Splinters and water scatter. Operatives hit the floor one by one.
Final attacker charges from behind. Barely shifting his stance, he drives the blade into the attacker’s shoulder — slow-motion crash through a table. Then silence. Only rain.
Last shot: low angle from the floor. He stands with his back to camera, surrounded by fallen operatives. He slowly sheathes his sword. Crimson coat shifts in the draft. Camera pulls to wide shot — rain falls soundlessly, atmosphere icy and razor-sharp. Hard freeze frame. Fade to black.

viral_video_prompts.text:
MOUNTAIN BIKE

## Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from a motorcycle rider on an extremely narrow, dangerous knife-edge mountain ridge. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Chrome cruiser handlebars, black fuel tank with a vintage logo, rider wearing black gloves and dark pants. The path is jagged white rock, barely wide enough for the bike. To the left is a steep green grassy drop-off; to the right is a sheer vertical cliff dropping into clouds and the deep blue ocean. Cinematic lighting, photorealistic, 4k, extreme vertigo, adrenaline atmosphere.

## Video Prompt:
The motorcycle drives forward at extreme high speed along the narrow rocky ridge. The camera moves forward at lightning-fast velocity, following the path with intense momentum. The bike suspension bounces violently over the uneven rocks. The view sweeps over the landscape at breakneck speed, with the clouds on the right blurring past and the green valley on the left a streak of motion. Maintain a stable but extremely dynamic action-camera feel. Ultra high speed, extreme adrenaline, perilous journey.

## 1. 🌋 Sports Car — Volcano Lava Fields
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from the driver’s seat of a low-slung supercar on an extremely narrow road cutting through active lava fields at night. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Carbon fiber steering wheel, glowing dashboard gauges, driver wearing red racing gloves. The road is cracked black basalt, barely wider than the car. To the left, rivers of glowing orange lava ooze toward the road; to the right, a field of hardened obsidian drops into a volcanic steam vent. Cinematic lighting from lava glow, photorealistic, 4K, extreme heat atmosphere, adrenaline tension.
Video Prompt:
The supercar accelerates at extreme speed along the narrow lava road. The camera surges forward with violent momentum, the cracked basalt blurring beneath. Glowing orange lava pulses and splashes on the left as the car roars past. Steam vents explode upward on the right. The dashboard rattles with vibration. The lava glow flickers intensely across the cockpit interior. Ultra high speed, extreme heat, volcanic danger, cinematic adrenaline atmosphere.

## 2. 🌿 Dirt Bike — Amazon Jungle Trail
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from a dirt bike rider on an extremely narrow, overgrown jungle trail cutting through the Amazon. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Knobby handlebars with orange grip tape, mud-caked number plate, rider wearing neon yellow gloves and armored pants. The path is dark wet mud and tangled roots, barely wide enough for the bike. To the left is a wall of dense green jungle; to the right is a sudden drop into a murky river below. Shafts of sunlight breaking through the canopy, photorealistic, 4K, sweat and humidity, adrenaline atmosphere.
Video Prompt:
The dirt bike tears forward at breakneck speed through the narrow jungle trail. The camera lurches violently as roots and rocks pound the suspension. Overhanging vines whip directly into the lens. Mud sprays in thick arcs from the rear tire. Light strobe flickers as the canopy breaks and closes above. The murky river on the right flashes in and out of view. Maintain raw, chaotic action-camera feel. Extreme speed, primal jungle energy, adrenaline chaos.

## 3. ❄️ Snowmobile — Arctic Cliff Edge
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from a snowmobile rider racing along a crumbling ice ledge above the Arctic Ocean. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Black rubber throttle grip, yellow snowmobile hood, rider wearing thick white arctic gloves and insulated black suit. The surface is jagged compacted snow and fractured ice. To the left is a flat tundra stretching to the horizon; to the right is a sheer ice cliff dropping hundreds of feet into a frozen grey ocean. Northern lights shimmer in the dark sky above. Photorealistic, 4K, biting cold atmosphere, extreme vertigo.
Video Prompt:
The snowmobile rockets forward along the crumbling ice ledge at extreme speed. The camera jolts with every crack and fracture in the ice surface. Ice chunks break off the cliff edge to the right, tumbling silently into the ocean below. The northern lights ripple and pulse overhead as the snowmobile tears through powdered snow clouds. Cold wind distorts the lens with frost particles. The tundra on the left blurs into a white streak. Ultra high speed, frozen abyss, survival energy, cinematic adrenaline.

## 4. 🏜️ ATV — Sahara Sand Dune Ridge
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from an ATV rider balanced on the razor-thin crest of a towering Sahara sand dune at golden hour. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Sand-worn handlebars with blue grips, dusty black fuel tank, rider wearing tan desert gloves and khaki pants. The path is the knife-thin peak of a massive dune, barely the width of the tires. To the left, a sheer vertical wall of cascading golden sand drops hundreds of feet; to the right, an endless orange desert valley stretches to the horizon. Sun blazing low on the horizon, photorealistic, 4K, scorching heat shimmer, adrenaline vertigo.
Video Prompt:
The ATV accelerates along the razor dune crest at terrifying speed. The camera teeters with every shift in balance, the drop on both sides blurring past in streaks of gold and orange. Sand explodes from the tires in rooster-tail plumes. The sun flares directly into the lens at the crest of each rise. The valley on the right shimmers with heat distortion. Cascading sand avalanches off the left edge in slow-motion contrast to the violent speed. Extreme velocity, desert vertigo, blazing cinematic light.

## 5. 🚵 Mountain Bike — Coastal Sea Cliff Path

To the left, a mossy stone wall rises steeply; to the right, the cliff drops vertically hundreds of feet into crashing turquoise Atlantic waves. Storm clouds rolling in the distance, photorealistic, 4K, wind-lashed atmosphere, extreme adrenaline.
Video Prompt:
The mountain bike plummets downhill at extreme speed along the ancient cliff path. The camera vibrates intensely as stone and loose gravel pound the tires. The turquoise ocean on the right roars far below, waves crashing against the cliff face. Wind buffets the lens violently. Stone walls on the left blur to grey streaks. The path twists and drops in rapid succession, the bike barely holding the edge. Spray from the ocean below mists the lens. Extreme descent, coastal vertigo, raw power, cinematic wind and sea.

## 6. 🚤 Speedboat — Amazon River Gorge
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from the cockpit of a racing speedboat threading through an extremely narrow river canyon deep in the Amazon. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Black throttle lever, fiberglass bow, driver wearing red waterproof gloves and a white helmet. The river is white water rapids, barely wider than the boat. To the left, a sheer red and orange sandstone canyon wall rises hundreds of feet; to the right, the same wall mirrors it, inches from the hull. Jungle vines and birds exploding from the walls above. Canyon walls on both sides blur into red and orange streaks. Birds scatter in explosion bursts from the walls above. The boat slams through rapids, the nose lifting and crashing with bone-jarring impact. Water sprays directly into the lens in thick white sheets. The gorge narrows and widens in rapid alternation. Ultra high speed, roaring water, canyon walls closing in, cinematic adrenaline chaos.

## 7. 🌙 Dune Buggy — Midnight Salt Flats
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from a dune buggy cockpit racing across the Salar de Uyuni salt flats at midnight. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Roll cage bars framing the view, knuckle-wrapped steering wheel, driver wearing black gloves. The ground is perfectly flat, mirror-like white salt reflecting an infinite star field below, merging seamlessly with the actual Milky Way above. The horizon line has completely dissolved. The buggy’s headlights are the only source of light for miles. Photorealistic, 4K, surreal infinite mirror atmosphere, existential adrenaline.
Video Prompt:
The dune buggy tears across the salt flats at extreme speed, stars above and below creating a total infinite mirror effect. The camera rockets forward through complete darkness, only the headlight beams cutting a path. Salt crystals spray from the tires into the beams like white sparks. The reflected Milky Way stretches in every direction, the horizon invisible. The engine screams in the silence. The buggy briefly catches air over a salt ridge, the stars spinning in all directions. Ultra high speed, infinite void, hypnotic surreal adrenaline.

## 8. 🐎 Horse — Mongolian Steppe Cliff Trail
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from a bareback rider gripping a black horse’s mane at full gallop along a narrow ancient trail carved into a Mongolian mountain ridge. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Both hands buried in thick black mane, no saddle or reins visible. The trail is hard pale dirt and loose shale. To the left, golden grasslands drop steeply into a vast steppe valley; to the right, jagged snow-capped peaks rise sharply. Wind whipping mane hair directly into the lens. Late afternoon golden hour light, photorealistic, 4K, raw primal energy, extreme adrenaline.
Video Prompt:
The horse gallops at full speed along the narrow ridge trail. The camera bucks and heaves with every powerful stride, the rhythm violent and organic. Mane hair whips repeatedly into the lens, partially obscuring the view in intense close-up blasts. The golden steppe valley on the left drops away with each stride. Loose shale scatters off the cliff edge under the hooves. Wind roars across the microphone. The jagged peaks on the right flash past in rapid succession. Raw, primal, unfiltered speed. No machine — pure animal power and survival energy.

## 9. ✈️ Fighter Jet — Storm Cell Dive
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from inside a fighter jet cockpit during a vertical dive into a massive Atlantic thunderstorm. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Heads-up display glowing green with altitude numbers spinning downward, gloved hands gripping the stick, oxygen mask visible at the bottom edge. The canopy is surrounded by a wall of grey-black storm clouds. Lightning detonates on both sides of the jet simultaneously. Rain streaks horizontally across the canopy at mach speed. Cinematic dramatic lighting from within the storm, photorealistic, 4K, terrifying scale, extreme adrenaline.
Video Prompt:
The fighter jet plunges vertically at mach speed directly into the storm cell. The camera slams downward with crushing G-force, the altimeter digits on the HUD spinning catastrophically. Lightning explodes in brilliant white flashes on all sides, illuminating the cockpit in strobing light. Cloud walls rush past at incomprehensible speed, forming a tunnel of grey and black. Rain hammers the canopy in a continuous deafening sheet. The aircraft vibrates violently as it punches through turbulence layers. Total sensory overload. Ultra high speed, lightning chaos, vertical dive into the abyss.

## 10. 🌊 Underwater Sled — Deep Ocean Trench Wall
Image Prompt:
First-person POV shot from a diver gripping an underwater propulsion sled, descending at high speed along the vertical face of a deep ocean trench wall. Wide-angle GoPro fisheye lens. Both hands gripping chrome handles, black wetsuit sleeves visible, depth gauge glowing on the wrist. The trench wall is jagged black volcanic rock covered in deep-sea coral and strange pale organisms. To the left, the wall rises to a dim blue surface glow far above; to the right, the trench drops into absolute crushing black darkness. Bioluminescent creatures flashing blue and green, photorealistic, 4K, deep sea dread, adrenaline claustrophobia.
Video Prompt:
The underwater sled accelerates downward along the trench wall at extreme speed, the wall rushing past in a blur of black rock and bioluminescent flashes. The camera dives with relentless downward momentum, the surface glow above rapidly shrinking to a faint blue sliver. Bioluminescent jellyfish and deep-sea creatures streak past the lens in explosive flashes of green, blue, and violet. Pressure bubbles stream from the sled in white trails. The darkness below grows denser and more absolute with every second. The trench wall tilts and curves. The abyss below has no bottom. Ultra depth, crushing silence, deep-sea terror.

viral_video_prompts.title: #409 VIRAL VIDEO PROMPT: Time Freeze .
viral_video_prompts.text:
Seedance 2.0 prompt:
Cinematic time-freeze short film, 15 seconds, ultra-realistic, Arri Alexa Mini shooting texture, 50mm lens, natural daylight hard shadows, shallow depth of field.

[0:00–0:03] Busy city sidewalk, normal time flow. Steadicam front-facing medium shot tracking: the main character walks confidently through the crowd. Pedestrians walk, check phones, chat; a flock of pigeons flies across the bright sunny sky in the distance. As he walks, he raises his right hand — and snaps his fingers.

[0:03–0:06] The instant of the snap — a powerful white spherical shockwave bursts from his fingertips, carrying visible air distortion and light refraction, spreading rapidly in all directions. It sweeps across the ground, kicking up dust and fallen leaves that freeze mid-air instantly. It sweeps over pedestrians — each one freezes mid-stride. It sweeps across the sky — every pigeon locks in a different wing-spread pose, hovering motionless in mid-air. The shockwave ripples a streak of light across distant building windows. After the shockwave vanishes — absolute silence. Subtle time-freeze particles float in the air, gently shimmering in the sunlight.

[0:06–0:09] In the silence, only the main character’s footsteps echo crisply. Camera flies backward ahead of him — he walks toward the lens, casually strolling through the frozen crowd, looking around this still world with a smug expression. He looks up and sees a pigeon hovering above, reaches out and gently strokes its feathers. The pigeon doesn’t move at all, like a sculpture, but lets out a deep coo that reverberates through the silence. Satisfied, he keeps walking.

[0:09–0:11] The main character walks up to a frozen young woman — she’s wearing a flowing red dress, her long hair caught by the wind and frozen mid-air in an elegant arc, one hand locked in a hair-tucking pose, expression graceful. He stops, hands in pockets, tilts his head and admires her. He comes around to face her, gives a slight nod with a corner smile, and whispers in english: “Are you hungry?”

[0:11–0:15] The main character turns around, reaches into his pant pocket and pulls out an oversized, comically giant lollipop — vivid swirling colors — and casually pops it into his mouth. With the giant lollipop in his mouth he turns to face the camera, smirks, raises his right hand and snaps again — a second shockwave, even more powerful, bursts outward from his fingertips in reverse, carrying air distortion and light refraction, spreading at high speed. Everything it touches instantly unfreezes: pedestrians resume walking, pigeons scatter flapping, the woman in the red dress continues tucking her hair and walks on completely unaware, fallen leaves finally land. City noise naturally returns. The main character, calmly turns and walks on. Camera slowly rises and pulls back into an overhead wide shot — his silhouette blends into the city. Fade to black.

Sound design: City noise → finger snap triggers a low-frequency explosive shockwave rumble radiating outward from near to far → absolute silence → footsteps echoing → pigeon cooing → whispered english “Are you hungry?” → exaggerated candy wrapper crinkle and lollipop pop sound → second finger snap → stronger reverse shockwave explosion rumble → city noise naturally restored.

viral_video_prompts.text:
## 🎬 How to Make Your Tom & Jerry Style Video
A super easy guide to create a fun video everyone will love! 🚀
With this guide, you will learn how to put cartoon characters (like a cat and mouse duo) into your video in a magical way. It’s so simple that it feels like playing!

## 🛠️ Tools You Will Use
You only need two tools (ask an adult to help you create accounts if needed):
- ChatGPT (with image generation) – to create the magic photos. 📸

- Kling AI or Grok Imagine – to turn the photos into a moving video. 🎥easemate+2

## 📸 STEP 1: Your Photos
You will need two types of photos:
- Your Photo
- Stand in front of a clean, plain wall.

- Look at the camera and give a soft smile.

- Ask someone to take the photo in good lighting so your face is clear.

- Cartoon Reference Photo
- Find a picture of a cartoon cat and mouse that you like (for example from a show, toy, or drawing).

- This photo will help ChatGPT create characters with the right look and style.linkedin+1

(If you want to stay safer with copyright, you can also use an original “cat and mouse” drawing instead of exact Tom & Jerry.)linkedin+1

## ✨ STEP 2: Create the Start Photo (in ChatGPT)
Now you will create the first image, where the characters are playing around you.
- Open ChatGPT in your browser.

- Click on the paperclip icon and upload:
- Your own photo

- The cartoon reference image (cat and mouse)

- Copy and paste this prompt exactly:

🖼️ PROMPT — START FRAME:
“Use the attached photo as a reference for the person’s face, features, and general appearance. Create a hyper-realistic photo composite. The person (matching the attached photo) has a calm and slightly amused expression. A 3D cartoon gray cat running across their left shoulder chasing a 3D cartoon small brown mouse running across their chest, both with playful expressions. Hyper-realistic photo composite, seamless blend, cinematic studio lighting, 4K, sharp focus. Also use the attached image of Tom and Jerry as reference for their appearance.”

- Save the generated image to your phone or computer.

## 😱 STEP 3: Create the Shock Photo (in ChatGPT)
Next, you will create the funny “scared” image where the characters catch you.
- In the same ChatGPT chat, copy and paste this prompt:

🖼️ PROMPT — END FRAME:
“Based on the previous image and the attached photo of the person, create the ‘End Frame’. The person (matching the attached photo) now has a shocked expression with eyes wide open. A 3D cartoon small brown mouse standing on their right shoulder stretching their lower lip sideways with both hands. A 3D cartoon gray cat sitting on top of their head pressing down with both paws holding them still, evil grin. Maintain the same hyper-realistic photo composite, seamless blend, cinematic studio lighting, 4K, sharp focus. Also use the attached image of Tom and Jerry as reference for their appearance.”

- Save this second image as well.

## 🎬 STEP 4: Make the Magic Video (with Kling AI or Grok)
Now you will turn the two images into a real animated clip. You can use Kling AI or Grok Imagine (both support image to video).pollo+2

## Option 1 – Using Kling AI
- Go to the Kling AI website and log in.

- Choose the AI Videos mode, then select Image to Video.

- In the first box (Start Frame), upload Image 1 (you with the calm, amused face).

- Add an End Frame and upload Image 2 (you with the shocked face).

- In the prompt box, paste this animation text:

🎬 PROMPT — ANIMATION:
“Fast-paced, rapid move, cartoon effect; The 3D cartoon gray cat and brown mouse are playfully chasing each other on the person’s shoulders, behind the neck, in circle. Suddenly, the mouse stops and pulls the person’s lip to the side, while the cat jumps on their head to hold them. The person’s expression change every time the cartoon move, and end it  from amused to pure shock. Smooth motion, realistic physics, 4K..”

- Set the duration to about 5 seconds, choose your aspect ratio, and click Generate.

## Option 2 – Using Grok Imagine
- Open the Grok app or website and go to the Imagine or Video section.

- Choose the image to video feature.

- Upload Image 1 as your starting frame and, if Grok allows, set Image 2 as the ending frame or upload both images and describe the transition between them.

- Paste the same animation prompt into Grok’s prompt box (you can keep the exact text from above).

- Set a short duration (around 5–10 seconds, depending on the options you see) and generate your video.

First Frame Image Prompt:
A first-person perspective POV shot of someone riding a rollercoaster at the top of a steep slope, about to drop. In the foreground at the bottom, two hands firmly grip a dark grey horizontal safety bar. Below the bar, grey sneakers with black laces rest on footrests. The rollercoaster track made of two parallel silver metal rails with dark ties is positioned at the peak of a dramatic incline, angled steeply downward ahead, creating a thrilling view of the imminent drop down the cliff face. The setting is a breathtaking coastal landscape on a bright sunny day. To the left, a steep dark grey rocky cliff drops down to a turquoise ocean with white crashing waves and light mist far below. To the right, lush vibrant green rolling hills and fields extend to the horizon. Clear bright blue sky with prominent sun glare and lens flare in the upper left. The track ahead plunges dramatically downward, emphasizing the height and the steep descent about to begin.

Image-to-Video Prompt:
Fast-paced thrilling first-person POV rollercoaster ride. Camera plunges dramatically into a steep near-vertical dive down a massive cliff covered in vibrant green moss. The coaster banks sharply to the right, following a curving track along the towering textured rock face with churning ocean far below on the left. Incredibly fast motion with motion blur on passing rocks and greenery, emphasizing intense speed and steep descent. Rider's hands remain firmly gripping the safety bar at the bottom throughout. Bright sunny lighting with occasional lens flares. Continuous smooth camera movement following the track's twists and turns against the dramatic coastal landscape.

In the foreground at the bottom, two gloved hands grip the edge of the rooftop ledge, knuckles forward. Below, grey parachute pack straps are partially visible at the lower frame. The rooftop ledge drops away into a sheer vertical glass and steel facade. Far below, a sprawling city grid stretches to the horizon — tiny cars, streets, and city blocks visible thousands of feet down. Overcast sky with soft diffused light and thin cloud layer at eye level. Light mist drifts at mid-height across the building facade. Cinematic wide angle, ultra-realistic, 4K.
🎬 Image-to-Video Prompt:
Fast first-person POV BASE jump off a glass skyscraper rooftop. Camera launches forward off the ledge and immediately enters freefall — the building facade rushes past vertically at extreme speed, glass and steel panels blurring. City grid below rapidly expands as altitude drops. Wind roars with full audio. Camera spins slightly as body tumbles in freefall, then stabilizes. Parachute deploys with a sharp jerk — camera yanks upward dramatically, sudden deceleration. The city below now visible in full panoramic width, drifting gently. Bright ambient light with motion blur on the building facade during freefall. Smooth continuous motion, hyper-realistic physics.

3.Surfing a Giant Wave
🖼️ First Frame Image Prompt:
A first-person perspective POV shot sitting on a surfboard in the open ocean, facing a massive rising wave. In the foreground at the bottom, two hands grip the sides of a white surfboard with teal graphic detail, arms outstretched. Bare feet visible at the lower frame on the tail of the board. Ahead, a towering 20-foot blue-green wave wall rises dramatically, white foam cresting and curling at the top, backlit by golden afternoon sunlight creating a translucent glow through the wave face. Ocean surface choppy and dark around the board. Clear sky visible above the wave crest. Ultra-realistic, cinematic wide angle, 4K, dramatic natural lighting.

Thrilling first-person POV surfing a massive open ocean wave. Camera drops into the steep wave face as the board accelerates down the wall — water rushes past on both sides at high speed. Surfer carves a hard right bank, spray shooting out from the rail. The wave barrel begins to close overhead, creating a tube of churning white water above. Sunlight refracts through the wave lip in slow-motion prismatic light, then the barrel closes. Camera bursts out of the tube into open white water, bright sunlight flooding the frame. Continuous smooth motion, natural wave physics, ocean sound design with rushing water and roaring impact. Hyper-realistic, cinematic.

## 4. Zip Line Jungle Canopy
🖼️ First Frame Image Prompt:
A first-person perspective POV shot gripping a zip line handle above a vast tropical jungle canopy. In the foreground at the top, both gloved hands grip a black and orange carabiner handle attached to a thick steel cable that extends diagonally forward and downward into the distance. Golden afternoon sunlight filters through the canopy edge, creating dramatic god rays. Mist drifts low over the treetops in the distance. Clear blue sky with scattered white clouds above. At center frame hangs Xu Beihong’s iconic ink-wash galloping horse scroll, rendered in traditional Chinese brushwork with bold, fluid strokes. The black stallion mid-gallop is physically breaking out of the canvas — its front hooves and chest piercing through the paper sudrface, ink splattering into the air as it crosses from 2D into the real world. The horse’s anatomy is lifelike and muscular, mane whipping fiercely. Video Prompt (Kling / Wan.video) — ~10 seconds:

[0–2s] The horse’s front hooves punch through the canvas, paper tearing with shreds flying. [4–6s] It rears up powerfully, mane and tail exploding in the air, ink droplets scattering like rain. [6–8s] The horse charges straight toward the camera in slow motion, eyes wild, nostrils flaring. [8–10s] Camera pulls back to reveal the torn empty frame still swaying on the museum wall.

[4–6s] Water rushes across the gallery floor in slow motion, soaking the red carpet runner. [6–8s] A visitor backs away in disbelief as water laps at their feet. [8–10s] The wave slowly recedes, pulling back into the frame — the painting hangs still again, dripping wet.

## 2. Da Vinci’s Vitruvian Man
Image Prompt:
A surreal yet photorealistic scene inside a Renaissance-style Florentine archive library — dark wood shelves, amber candlelight, aged stone walls. Da Vinci’s Vitruvian Man sketch is pinned on an illuminated study table. The figure is stepping off the aged parchment — one foot planted on the wooden table surface, the other still sketched in pencil on paper. His body transitions from faded ink line drawing to full anatomically detailed human form in golden warm skin tones. Unreal Engine 5, 8K resolution, volumetric candlelight, cinematic color grading, sharp focus, masterpiece quality.

Video Prompt:
Camera closes in slowly on Da Vinci’s Vitruvian Man pinned to a wooden archive table, lit by warm amber light. [0–2s] The figure’s pencil lines begin to glow faintly, then move — arms shifting from the classic spread pose. [2–4s] The figure peels away from the parchment, rising upright, transforming from flat sketch into a lifelike 3D human form on the table. [4–6s] He stretches his arms wide, then raises them overhead, showing the perfect golden-ratio proportions. [6–8s] He looks down at his own hands — turning them over in wonder. [8–10s] He steps back onto the page and dissolves back into pencil lines, the parchment lying flat and still.

## 3. Van Gogh’s Starry Night
Image Prompt:
A breathtaking surreal scene inside a grand European art museum with vaulted ceilings and carved stone pillars. Van Gogh’s Starry Night hangs on the central wall. The swirling blue and gold stars are physically bleeding out of the canvas — spiraling vortexes of luminous paint expanding into the museum air like living nebulas, painting the ceiling in swirling gold and midnight blue. Unreal Engine 5, 8K resolution, bioluminescent lighting, dynamic paint particle effects, cinematic color grading, immersive environment, masterpiece quality.

[2–4s] The vortex explodes outward from the canvas — swirling spirals of blue and gold light fill the museum ceiling like a living aurora. [6–8s] The entire ceiling becomes the night sky — deep blue, stars spinning. [8–10s] Everything pulls back like a reverse explosion, collapsing back into the canvas. ## 4. Qi Baishi’s Shrimp Painting

A surreal hyper-realistic scene inside a traditional Chinese ink painting gallery — bamboo-panelled walls, soft diffused daylight, pale stone floors. [6–8s] Camera pushes close to the glass — a shrimp swims directly toward the lens, eyes catching the light. [8–10s] Camera pulls back to show the scroll now blank — all the shrimp swimming freely in the tank.

## 5. Picasso’s Guernica
Image Prompt:
A dramatic surreal scene inside a modern art museum with raw concrete walls and industrial lighting. Picasso’s Guernica hangs as a massive black-and-white canvas. Fragmented cubist figures are physically stepping out of the canvas — fractured geometric human and animal forms existing in 3D space in stark monochrome, their edges still splintered like broken glass. Video Prompt:
Camera holds wide on Guernica’s massive monochrome canvas in a concrete museum hall. [0–2s] The painted figures begin to tremble — cracks form along the canvas surface. [2–4s] Cubist geometric figures break through the canvas edge — fragmented arms, a screaming face, a horse’s broken head emerging in stark 3D black and white. [8–10s] A violent magnetic pull drags all the fragments back into the canvas simultaneously — the painting seals itself. Still. Silent.

## 6. Chinese Dragon Scroll

A spectacular surreal scene inside the Palace Museum (Forbidden City) grand hall — red lacquered columns, golden imperial décor, sweeping curved roof beams. A traditional Chinese ink-wash dragon hanging scroll is mounted on the central wall. The coiled dragon is bursting free — its serpentine body spiraling out of the silk scroll into the physical hall, scales glinting with gold and black ink, claws raking the air, whiskers flowing. Golden mist trails from its mouth as it loops around a red lacquered column. Unreal Engine 5, 8K resolution, imperial golden lighting, volumetric mist, cinematic color grading, masterpiece quality.

Video Prompt:

[0–2s] The ink dragon begins to stir — its coiled form shifting, scales rippling like water. [4–6s] Its full serpentine body spirals out and loops majestically around a red lacquered column, gold and black scales catching the light. [6–8s] It breathes out a plume of golden mist that drifts through the hall. [8–10s] The dragon turns and glides back into the torn scroll — the silk repairs itself seamlessly. The hall falls silent.

## 7. Japanese Ukiyo-e Tiger
Image Prompt:
A stunning surreal scene inside a high-end Tokyo auction house — polished dark wood panels, warm amber spotlights, white glove staff. A bold Edo-period Japanese woodblock print of a crouching tiger is displayed on an auction easel. The tiger is leaping off the flat print — its body transitioning from flat graphic ukiyo-e ink and woodblock texture into a fully muscular, anatomically real Bengal tiger landing on the tatami floor. [2–4s] The tiger crouches and then leaps off the print — flat graphic form transforming mid-air into a fully real Bengal tiger, landing silently on the tatami floor. [4–6s] It pads slowly forward, each paw placed deliberately — real fur, amber eyes glowing. [6–8s] It turns and faces the camera, holding eye contact, breath visible. [8–10s] It dissolves from the tips of its fur backward — becoming flat ink again, the woodblock print hanging perfectly still on the easel.

In an instant, frozen time and gravity seemed to explode with this subtle gesture. 💡 Pro Tips:
Free doesn't mean limited anymore. Most free tools now offer 80-90% of paid features because competition is fierce. Companies bet on converting 5% of free users to paid, so they keep free tiers generous. Use multiple free tools simultaneously instead of one expensive all-in-one solution. Set calendar reminders every 3 months to check for new free alternatives that just launched.

Software companies rely on subscription fatigue and switching friction to keep overcharging. They know most people won't take 20 minutes to test alternatives. 💰 Bottom Line:
Add up your current monthly subscriptions. Multiply by 12. That's your annual software cost. Most people spend $3,000-8,000 yearly on tools they could replace for free. Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

Prompt:
Professional character design sheet with realistic photography style, pure white background, 2K resolution. The character is a young Asian male with the following features:

**HEAD DETAILS SECTION:**
- Front view of head without accessories
- Right side view of head without accessories
- Front view of head with full outfit and accessories
- Right side view of head with full outfit and accessories
All head views must have identical facial features, skin tone, proportions, and no perspective distortion. The character has:
- Large round eyes with brown irises
- Thick dark eyebrows slightly arched
- Small nose with slightly upturned tip
- Wide smile showing white teeth
- Full round cheeks
- Warm-toned skin, light to medium complexion
- Black hair with undercut style: short on sides and back, longer and voluminous on top with upward texture

**FULL BODY ORTHOGRAPHIC SECTION:**
5 full body views arranged horizontally:
- Front view
- Left 45-degree side view
- Right side view
- Right 45-degree side view
- Back view
All views must be equal width and height, orthographic projection with no perspective distortion. The character wears:
- White polo shirt with red and white (or red deep blue) striped collar
- Red laurel wreath logo on left chest (similar to Fred Perry)
- Silver ring on right index finger
- Gold watch face with brown strap on left wrist
Standard neutral natural standing pose, full body in frame, arms naturally hanging at sides, no extra movements

**SUPPLEMENTARY VIEWS SECTION:**
- Half-body side view
- Top-down overhead view
- Bottom-up under view
Character, outfit, and proportions must match main views exactly

**MATERIAL DETAIL SECTION:**
Extreme close-up shots of:
- Fabric texture of clothing
- Shoe and boot details
Clear display of material patterns, textures, and details

**OVERALL CONSISTENCY REQUIREMENTS:**
- All modules show the same character with identical facial features, height, body type, outfit, accessories, lighting, and materials
- High precision, maximum detail, cinematic animation character design standard
- Professional photography lighting with soft shadows
- Clean white background
- No overlapping or cropping of modules
- Clear and standardized layout

The design sheet should be organized in a grid layout with clear spacing between sections, professional character design sheet format.🚨 STOP Wasting Hours on Broken AI Videos! 🚨

Your character's face keeps changing in every scene?
Hair color shifting? Outfit morphing?
You're not alone. 95% of AI creators face this nightmare.

Here's what the pros DON'T tell you:

The secret isn't the AI tool. It's the CHARACTER CONSISTENCY DESIGN SHEET.

Think of it like this:
Without a design sheet = Telling 10 different artists to "draw a girl"
With a design sheet = Giving them the EXACT blueprint

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📐 WHAT'S IN A CHARACTER CONSISTENCY DESIGN SHEET?

1️⃣ TURNING DIAGRAM (3 angles)
• Front view - full body
• Side view - profile
• Back view - all details

2️⃣ FACIAL EXPRESSIONS (6 emotions)
• Neutral, Joy, Sadness
• Anger, Surprise, Fear

3️⃣ POSE CHART (4 action shots)
• Running, Jumping
• Laughing, Crying

All on ONE reference sheet. Same character. Zero morphing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 WHY THIS WORKS:

AI tools like Kling, Runway, Meta AI, and Google Veo read your reference image.
Multiple angles + expressions = The AI "learns" your character.
Result? Same face, same outfit, every single time.

Pro creators use this for:
✅ Faceless YouTube channels
✅ AI animated shorts
✅ Viral TikTok/Instagram content
✅ Storytelling videos
✅ Character-based content series

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 PRO TIPS:

• Use SEED CONSISTENCY - lock the same seed number across all your video generations
• Start with IMAGE-TO-VIDEO instead of text prompts for 10x better consistency
• Generate your design sheet FIRST before making any videos
• Keep character description identical in every prompt - copy/paste the exact same wording
• Use neutral gray background on your design sheet so AI focuses on the character, not scenery

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 THE TRUTH:

Most people skip this step because they want quick results.
Then they spend 10x more time fixing broken videos.
Smart creators invest 30 minutes upfront. Save 20+ hours later.

The difference between amateur AI content and professional?
It's not talent. It's systems.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚡ QUICK START (Do this today):

1. Generate or upload your character image
2. Use AI to create turnaround views (front/side/back)
3. Add 6 facial expression variations
4. Add 4 action pose variations
5. Save as ONE master reference sheet
6. Feed this sheet to your video AI tool
7. Watch the magic happen

Time invested: 30-45 minutes
Time saved: Forever

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

✅ BOTTOM LINE:

If you want consistent AI videos that actually work, you need a Character Consistency Design Sheet BEFORE you generate anything.

No more face morphing.
No more outfit changes.
No more starting over.

Just clean, consistent, professional AI content every time.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

P.S. This works with ALL major AI tools:
ChatGPT, Midjourney, Leonardo AI, Kling, Runway, Meta AI, Google Veo, Stable Diffusion, Flux.

Stop fighting with inconsistent characters. Start with the blueprint. 🎬

Free Video Editing Apps 2026
That Real Creators Actually Use

📱 1. CapCut — The King of Creator Apps
- -

There’s a reason why millions of creators worldwide can’t stop using CapCut
• Free editing, music, effects, filters — all built-in
• Perfect for TikTok / Reels / YouTube Shorts sizing
• So easy, you’ll make your first video in under 5 minutes
• AI auto-captions now in 40+ languages with 95% accuracy
• Smart background removal without green screen
• Trending effects library updated weekly with viral templates
• Keyframe animation for smooth transitions
• Speed curves for dramatic slow-mo and time-lapse effects
• Text-to-speech with natural-sounding voices
• Cloud storage lets you edit across multiple devices
✅ Best for beginners to intermediate creators
Why it’s winning: Owned by TikTok, packed with pro features that rival desktop software. The algorithm integration means your videos sync perfectly with platform requirements.
Best use cases: Dance videos, lip-sync content, product showcases, quick trending clips

Link

🎬 2. VN Video Editor — Free But Feels Premium
- -

VN is the free app with features that should cost money
• Multi-track audio support (rare in free apps) — layer up to 99 tracks
• Frame-by-frame control — more precise than CapCut
• Easy voiceover and sound mixing with volume curves
• Keyframe animations for position, scale, rotation, and opacity
• Curve speed adjustment for cinematic effects
• Masking tools to create unique visual effects
• Picture-in-picture with unlimited layers
• Color grading with LUTs (professional color filters)
• Export in 4K resolution without compression
• No forced watermark — completely clean exports
• Supports all video formats including MOV, MP4, AVI
Perfect if you want to create:
📚 Tutorial videos, product reviews, vlogs, YouTube-style content, documentary-style edits, mini-films
Pro tip: VN’s timeline interface is closer to desktop editors, making it easier to transition to Premiere Pro or Final Cut later

📲 Download:
https://www.vlognow.me/

✂️ 3. InShot — The Speed Demon
- -

Not as famous as CapCut, but InShot is still a creator favorite
• Fastest editing workflow — seriously quick, trim videos in seconds
• Beautiful text and sticker options with 100+ font styles
• Supports multiple aspect ratios (1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9) — switch instantly
• NEW: AI speed-ramp detects dramatic moments automatically
• Pre-made transitions that look professional
• Music library with beat-sync feature for perfect timing
• Video filters with adjustable intensity
• Collage maker for split-screen effects
• Built-in stock footage and photo integration
• One-tap background blur for portrait videos
• Reverse video effect for creative loops
• Audio fade in/fade out with precision control
The interface is super simple, perfect for fast product videos and quick posts. You can edit a 60-second Reel in under 10 minutes once you get the hang of it.
Best use cases: E-commerce videos, before/after reveals, quick tutorials, motivational quotes with visuals

📲 Download:
https://inshot.com/

🎥 4. VLLO — Simple But Powerful
- -

For creators who want pro results without the complexity
• Excellent voiceover recording with noise reduction built-in
• Ready-made templates included (updated monthly with trending styles)
• Smooth, fluid interface that doesn’t lag on older phones
• Watermark-free export even on free version
• Transition effects with duration control
• Video speed adjustment from 0.25x to 4x
• Background music library with commercial-use tracks
• Mosaic blur for privacy (blur faces, license plates, etc.)
• Duplicate/copy clips instantly for pattern effects
• Freeze frame feature for dramatic pauses
• Video rotation and flip with one tap
• Audio extraction from video files
• PIP (Picture-in-Picture) with adjustable sizing
Best for: People who want to “look professional” without the learning curve. VLLO strikes the perfect balance between simple and capable.
Ideal content types: Travel vlogs, daily life videos, small business promos, talking-head content, educational videos

📲 Download:https://www.vllo.io/

⚡ 5. KineMaster — Mobile Pro Power (With Catch)
- -

KineMaster is the “desktop replacement” for mobile
• Multiple video layers — stack up to 10 video clips simultaneously
• Chroma key (green screen removal) with edge refinement
• Tons of effects and tools — over 2,500 built-in assets
• Updated 2026 version runs smoother on budget phones (50% faster rendering)
• Blending modes like Overlay, Screen, Multiply for creative compositing
• Audio mixer with EQ controls and audio ducking
• Instant preview without rendering lag
• Asset store with premium transitions, effects, and fonts
• Volume envelope for precise audio control
• 3D transitions for professional-looking scene changes
• Color adjustment with HSL curves
• Export up to 4K 60fps on supported devices
• Project management system to organize multiple edits
❗ Downside: Free version has watermark (premium unlocks everything at $4.99/month)
Best for: Creators who need detailed control beyond basic free apps. If you’re serious about mobile editing and want maximum flexibility, KineMaster is worth the subscription.
Perfect for: Short films, music videos, promotional content, real estate videos, YouTube documentaries

📲 Download:https://www.kinemaster.com/

🎞️ 6. YouTube Create — YouTube’s Official Editor
- -

Adding this because YouTube built their own editing tool
• Fast editing specifically for YouTube Shorts with optimized export settings
• Access to YouTube’s copyright-free music library (10,000+ tracks)
• Upload directly to your channel — no extra steps, saves phone storage
• NEW 2026: AI video generation powered by Google Veo for B-roll creation
• Auto audio cleanup removes background noise with one tap
• Beat-matching feature syncs cuts to music automatically
• Filters and effects designed for mobile-first viewing
• Auto-reframe keeps subjects centered when cropping
• Captions with YouTube’s industry-leading speech recognition
• Trending sounds integration shows what’s viral right now
• Voiceover recording with studio-quality processing
• Intro/outro templates branded for your channel
• Analytics preview shows estimated engagement before posting
Perfect for YouTube Shorts creators who want speed and convenience. The direct integration means your videos upload faster and maintain quality better than third-party apps.
Use cases: Commentary videos, reaction content, how-to shorts, channel teasers, community updates

📲 Download:https://www.youtube.com/creators/youtube-create/

🎁 BONUS: Instagram Edits — Meta's Answer to CapCut
- -

Instagram finally launched their own standalone editing app
• Built specifically for Reels creators by Instagram
• Seamless integration with Instagram and Facebook
• Cloud-based project saving across devices
• AI-powered smart editing suggests cuts based on music beats
• Access to Instagram's trending audio library before it goes public
• Advanced color grading tools with presets from top creators
• Multi-track timeline for complex edits
• Green screen effects and background replacement
• Text animations synced to audio
• Collaboration features — share projects with other creators
• Draft ideas tracker to plan content calendar
• Performance insights show best posting times
• Direct publish to Reels with optimal compression
• Camera tools built-in for recording and editing in one place
• Trending hashtag suggestions based on your content
Why it matters: Instagram prioritizes videos edited with their app in the algorithm. If you're serious about Reels growth, this gives you a platform advantage.
Best for: Instagram-first creators, influencers, brands focusing on Reels, anyone who wants algorithmic boost
Use cases: Instagram Reels, Facebook Reels, Stories content, carousel videos, brand collaborations
📲 Download:
https://creators.instagram.com/edits

💡 Pro Tips
• CapCut + InShot combo = unbeatable workflow for most creators (use CapCut for effects, InShot for speed)
• Always export in highest quality your phone allows (file size doesn't matter anymore with fast internet)
• Use auto-captions — they boost watch time by 28% and help with accessibility
• Vertical video (9:16) is dominating 2026 — hook viewers in first 3 seconds or they'll scroll
• Edit on WiFi, post on data — rendering drains battery fast
• Keep original files for 30 days in case you need to re-edit

🎯 The Truth
Most viral creators don't use expensive software. They master ONE free app deeply instead of jumping between tools. Pick one, learn it completely, then move up. The app matters less than your consistency and storytelling. A perfectly edited boring video still flops. An okay-edited compelling story goes viral.

⚡ Quick Start
1. Download CapCut (easiest) or VN (most features)
2. Edit one 15-second video today — pick any topic
3. Post it — even if imperfect, done is better than perfect
4. Repeat daily for 30 days and watch your skills explode
5. Join creator communities to see what others are making

🔥 Bottom Line
You don't need money to create viral content in 2026. You need consistency, the right free tool, and willingness to learn. Every big creator started with free apps. Your turn starts now. The difference between you and successful creators isn't talent or budget — it's that they posted 100 videos while you're still planning your first one.

The AI prediction model needs consistent data to understand your content. One post per week = not enough signals. The algorithm literally forgets you between posts.
Research shows: Pages posting once weekly get 40% less engagement than daily posters.

- Content seen mostly by current followers

You’re posting just enough to avoid being forgotten, but not enough to trigger the “discovery mode.” The algorithm keeps you in your existing bubble.

You’re building momentum, but haven’t peaked yet.

Don’t start by asking it to write code.
Instead, begin with:
“Here is the repo. Help me understand it. Show me:
• Main entry points
• Important folders
• Key files related to feature X”

Claude will scan files, run commands, and build a mental map of your project. You’ll get a clear, human explanation of codebases you didn’t even write.

### Step 2: Force It to Plan
Once it understands the project, ask:
“Based on what you saw, plan how to add feature X.
List the steps, files to edit, and commands we’ll need to run.”

This step is where most people fail — and where Claude Code becomes dangerous (in a good way). You get a proper roadmap instead of chaotic code.

### Step 3: Let It Execute
Now tell it:
“Follow the plan. Make the edits. Show every diff and explain what changed and why.”

Claude will open files, edit code, run tests or build commands, and show you clean diffs.

### Step 4: Verify and Iterate
Never trust the first output. Use this loop:
- “Run the tests again”

- “Show me the logs”

other_posts.title: NotebookLM can help you turn messy lecture notes into a full exam study guide in under 5 minutes. Here are 7 prompts to go from confused and unprepared to exam-ready tonight:
other_posts.text:
#
- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

Most people open it, paste some notes, and ask basic questions.
The smart ones use these 7 prompts to turn it into a personal tutor that actually prepares them for exams — not just summarises things.
🔖 Save this before your next exam.

## 1/ The Lecture Note Processor
Upload your messy notes. Paste this:
“You are my professor and personal study coach. I just attended a lecture and took rough notes. Your job is to transform them into a clean, exam-ready study guide I can actually use tonight.
GOAL: Turn my messy lecture notes into a structured, easy-to-study guide.
CONTEXT:
- Subject: [subject name]

- Lecture topic: [topic]

- My notes: [paste notes here or upload file]

- Exam type: [MCQ / essay / problem-solving / mixed]

CONSTRAINTS:
- Use simple language — explain like I’m smart but new to this topic

- Do NOT repeat information — every section must add something new

- Flag anything unclear or missing from my notes that I should follow up on

- Cite which part of my uploaded notes each point comes from

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Main Ideas — the 5–7 most important points in plain English
Key Terms — definitions in one sentence each
How Ideas Connect — what leads to what, what builds on what
Real-Life Examples — 3 examples of this topic used in the real world
Common Student Mistakes — what gets people wrong and why
Memory Tricks — mnemonics, short stories, or analogies to lock it in
Practice Questions — 5 questions with full answers
Gaps in My Notes — what is missing or unclear that I should ask my teacher”

## 2/ The Textbook Chapter Breakdown
Upload the chapter PDF. Paste this:
“You are my exam tutor. This textbook chapter is dense and I need to understand it deeply — not just skim it — before my exam.
GOAL: Break this chapter down into everything I need to understand, apply, and remember for the exam.
CONTEXT:
- Subject: [subject]

- Chapter title or topic: [title]

- My exam is in: [X days]

- My current understanding: [zero / basic / moderate]

CONSTRAINTS:
- Prioritise what’s most likely to appear in exams — not just everything equally

- Use the source material only — do not add outside information

- For the hardest concept, explain it like I am 12 years old

- Connect this chapter to what came before it in the course

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Chapter in 3 Sentences — the simplest possible overview
What I Should Know After This — 5 clear learning goals
Topic Map — main topics → subtopics → key details in a clean list
Formulas or Frameworks — when to use each one and why
The 3 Hardest Concepts — why they’re tricky and how to get them right
ELI12 Explanation — the hardest idea explained in everyday language
Connection to Previous Chapters — how this builds on earlier content
Worked Example — one problem solved step by step with explanation per step
10-Bullet Revision Summary — the whole chapter in 10 short points”

## 3/ The Exam Question Predictor
Upload your syllabus, notes, or past papers. Paste this:
“You are an exam setter who also coaches students. You know exactly how exams are designed. Based only on my uploaded course materials, predict what will come in my exam and build a preparation plan.
GOAL: Tell me what is most likely to appear in my exam and exactly how to prepare for it.
CONTEXT:
- Course name: [course name]

- Exam format: [MCQ / short answer / essay / numerical / case study / mixed]

- Exam date: [date]

- Topics I feel least confident about: [list them]

CONSTRAINTS:
- Base all predictions only on my uploaded materials — no guessing

- Rank topics by probability of appearing, not just importance

- Be brutally honest about which topics are high risk

- Include at least one ‘trick question’ style prediction per major topic

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Top 10 Exam Topics — ranked by likelihood of appearing, with reason
Question Types by Topic — MCQ / short / long / numerical / case study
Difficulty Level by Topic — memory-based / application / deep analysis
15 Realistic Exam Questions — labelled easy / medium / hard
Full Model Answers with Marking Notes — where marks are typically lost
Top Student Mistakes — by topic, with how to avoid each one
Time Strategy — how many minutes to spend per section
Priority Study Order — what to study first based on marks, difficulty, and my weak areas”

## 4/ Explain a Difficult Concept Until I Get It
Paste this whenever you’re stuck:
“You are the best teacher I’ve ever had — the kind who never gives up until the student truly understands. I am confused about a concept and I need you to explain it from multiple angles until it fully clicks.
GOAL: Help me deeply understand one concept — not just memorise a definition.
CONTEXT:
- Concept I’m stuck on: [concept / formula / topic]

- Subject: [subject]

- What I already understand: [describe or say ‘nothing yet’]

- What confuses me most: [describe the specific part that doesn’t make sense]

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT use jargon in the first explanation — save technical terms for later

- Each explanation must use a completely different approach

- Connect it to something I already know from everyday life

- Do not move on until the simple version is clear first

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Plain English Explanation — zero jargon, maximum clarity
Textbook Explanation — correct academic language I can use in exams
Visual Description — what a diagram or flowchart of this would look like
Real-Life Analogy — a story or comparison that makes it ‘click’
Step-by-Step Breakdown — if there’s a formula or process, each step explained and why
Why It Matters — what problem this concept solves in the real world
Where Students Go Wrong — the 3 most common confusion points
3 Application Scenarios — situations where I must use this concept, with worked examples
Link to Basics — how this connects to a simpler idea I already know”

## 5/ The Flashcard Generator (Study Faster, Remember Longer)
Upload your study material. Paste this:
“You are a learning scientist who designs flashcard systems based on spaced repetition and active recall — the two most proven study techniques in memory research.
GOAL: Build a complete flashcard set that helps me retain this topic long-term, not just overnight.
CONTEXT:
- Topic or subject: [topic]

- My exam is in: [X days / weeks]

- Study app I use: [Anki / Quizlet / paper / other]

- Hardest parts for me: [list or say ‘unsure’]

CONSTRAINTS:
- Mix question types — no more than 40% should be simple definitions

Short punchy takes perform best here.
Reply to others. Join conversations. Post threads.
The more you show up, the more the algorithm pushes you out.

Long videos build trust and watch time.
Batch film shorts in one go to save time.

other_posts.title: 20 Free Tools To Start A Business (And How To Use Each One)
other_posts.text:
Zero budget. Zero
 excuses. Just start.
Most people think starting a business requires a big investment. It does not. Every tool on this list is completely free. Here is how to use each one.
- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

## 1. You Need a Brand — Instagram is Free
🔗 instagram.com
What it does: Build your personal brand with posts, Reels, and Stories. Your Instagram IS your portfolio and your storefront.
Quick Start: Set up your bio with one clear sentence about who you help, post one piece of content today, and use a niche hashtag.
Pro Tip: Treat your Instagram like a business card. Every post should reflect who you are and what you stand for.

## 2. You Need Graphic Design — Canva is Free
🔗 canva.com
What it does: Create posts, logos, banners, and presentations without any design skills. Thousands of templates are ready to go.
Quick Start: Pick a template, swap the text and colors, and download in under 5 minutes.
Pro Tip: Use Canva’s Brand Kit to keep your colors and fonts consistent across every piece of content you create.

## 3. You Need a Website — Carrd is Free
🔗 carrd.co
What it does: Build a clean, fast one-page website or landing page in minutes. No coding needed.
Quick Start: Pick a template, add your name, links, and one call to action, then hit publish.
Pro Tip: Use Carrd as your link-in-bio page to send followers to all your offers and platforms in one place.

## 4. You Need Email Marketing — MailerLite is Free
🔗 mailerlite.com
What it does: Send newsletters, set up automations, and collect up to 500 subscribers completely free.
Quick Start: Create a simple signup form, embed it on your Carrd site, and send your first welcome email.
Pro Tip: Email subscribers are YOURS. Social media followers can disappear overnight. Build your list from day one.

## 5. You Need an AI Writer — ChatGPT is Free
🔗 chatgpt.com
What it does: Write captions, emails, blog posts, scripts, and business ideas on demand in seconds.
Quick Start: Type “write me 5 Facebook post ideas about [your niche]” and pick the best one to publish today.
Pro Tip: The better your prompt, the better the output. Always tell ChatGPT your audience, tone, and goal.

## 6. You Need to Go Viral — VidIQ is Free
🔗 vidiq.com
What it does: Keyword research, video analytics, and daily content ideas for YouTube and social media growth.
Quick Start: Install the free Chrome extension and analyze your top competitors’ best performing videos.
Pro Tip: Use VidIQ to find low-competition keywords your audience is already searching for. Let data drive your content strategy.

## 7. You Need a Store — Ko-Fi is Free
🔗 ko-fi.com
What it does: Sell digital products, memberships, and accept tips with zero setup fees and no monthly charges.
Quick Start: Create your page, upload one digital product such as a PDF, guide, or template, and share the link everywhere.
Pro Tip: Start with one simple digital product. You do not need 10 products to make your first sale.

## 8. You Need to Accept Payment — Stripe is Free
🔗 stripe.com
What it does: Accept credit cards and online payments globally with no monthly fee whatsoever.
Quick Start: Create your account, connect it to Ko-Fi or your website, and you are ready to receive payments.
Pro Tip: Stripe only charges a small percentage per transaction. No sale, no fee. It is perfect for anyone just starting out.

## 9. You Need Project Management — Trello is Free
🔗 trello.com
What it does: Organize tasks, projects, and ideas using simple drag-and-drop boards and cards.
Quick Start: Create one board called “My Business”, add three columns: To Do, Doing, and Done. Start filling it in.
Pro Tip: Treat your content calendar like a project. Plan two weeks ahead and you will never run out of ideas again.

## 10. You Need Automation — Make is Free
🔗 make.com
What it does: Connect your apps and automate repetitive tasks without writing a single line of code.
Quick Start: Try a simple automation like “when I get a new email subscriber, add them to a Google Sheet” as your first workflow.
Pro Tip: Automate the tasks you do every single day first. Even saving 30 minutes daily compounds into massive time savings over a year.

## 11. You Need Accounting — Wave is Free
🔗 waveapps.com
What it does: Track income and expenses, send professional invoices, and manage your business finances for free.
Quick Start: Create your account, add your first income source, and log your first expense today.
Pro Tip: Track everything from day one. Good financial habits early means zero stress when tax time comes around.

## 12. You Need a CRM — HubSpot CRM is Free
🔗 hubspot.com/crm
What it does: Manage contacts, track leads, and follow up with potential clients all in one organized place.
Quick Start: Add your first 10 contacts and set a reminder to follow up with each one this week.
Pro Tip: Your network is your net worth. A CRM turns random connections into real, trackable business relationships.

## 13. You Need Time Tracking — Toggl is Free
🔗 toggl.com
What it does: Track exactly where your time goes each day across different projects and tasks.
Quick Start: Start a timer every time you begin a task. Review where your time went every Sunday evening.
Pro Tip: Most people waste 2 to 3 hours daily without realizing it. Toggl makes the truth impossible to ignore.

## 14. You Need AI Training — Sifu Yik is Free
🔗 https://sifuyik.substack.com/p/day-1-best-ai-model-sifu-yiks-5-day
What it does: Learn AI tools, content creation strategies, and how to build a business using free tools through daily posts and guides.
Quick Start: Follow the page, save the posts, and apply one thing you learn every single day without fail.
Pro Tip: The fastest way to learn is to apply, not just watch. One action beats ten saved posts that you never act on.

## 15. You Need a Workspace — Notion is Free
🔗 notion.so
What it does: Organize your notes, plans, SOPs, content ideas, and business systems all in one clean place.
Quick Start: Create one page called “My Business Hub” and start collecting all your ideas, plans, and goals there.
Pro Tip: Build a simple content calendar inside Notion to plan your posts one week in advance. It changes everything.

## 16. You Need Surveys — Tally is Free
🔗 tally.so
What it does: Build beautiful, unlimited forms and surveys with no paywalls, no limits, and no watermarks.
Quick Start: Create a one-question audience survey and share it in your next post or story today.
Pro Tip: Ask your audience what they struggle with the most. Their answers become your best content ideas and product ideas.

## 17. You Need a Logo — Namelix is Free
🔗 namelix.com
What it does: AI generates business names and logo ideas instantly based on the keywords you type in.
Quick Start: Type your niche keywords, browse the generated results, and download your favorite in PNG or SVG format.
Pro Tip: Do not spend weeks obsessing over a logo. Get something clean, start building your business, and refine it later.

## 18. You Need a Blog — Substack is Free
🔗 substack.com
What it does: Write and send newsletters, build a loyal audience, and even charge for premium content when you are ready.
Quick Start: Set up your publication in 10 minutes, write your first post, and share the link on all your social profiles.
Pro Tip: Repurpose your best Facebook posts into Substack newsletters. Same content, double the reach, zero extra effort.

## 19. You Need Presentations — NotebookLM is Free
🔗 notebooklm.google.com
What it does: Google’s AI tool that turns your documents, PDFs, and notes into polished slide decks and summaries automatically.
Quick Start: Upload any document or paste your notes, click “Generate Presentation”, and watch the AI handle the rest.
Pro Tip: Turn your best Substack posts into slide presentations for LinkedIn and Instagram carousels. One piece of content becomes many.

## 20. You Need Analytics — Google Analytics is Free
🔗 analytics.google.com
What it does: Track who visits your website, where they come from, what they click on, and how long they stay.
Quick Start: Connect it to your Carrd website and check your traffic report every Monday morning.
Pro Tip: Data tells the truth. Post more of what works and drop what does not. Let the numbers guide every decision.

## Overall Pro Tips
- Do not try all 20 tools at once. Master 3 to 5 first before adding more.

- Free tools are more than powerful enough to get your first customer.

- Stack them together: Instagram + Canva + Carrd + MailerLite + Ko-Fi = a complete business system.

- Consistency beats perfection. Show up every day, even when the output is not perfect.

- The best tool is the one you actually open and use.

## The Truth
Most people bookmark posts like this and do nothing.
The tools are not the problem. Starting is the problem.
You now have every tool, every link, and every action step you need. The only thing left is the decision to begin.

## Quick Start Plan (5 Days)
- Day 1: Set up Instagram + Canva + Notion

- Day 2: Build your website on Carrd

- Day 3: Start your email list on MailerLite

- Day 4: List your first offer on Ko-Fi

- Day 5: Learn AI for free with Sifu Yik

## Bottom Line
You do not need money to start a business.
You need a decision.
Pick one tool from this list. Open it right now. Take one action today. Build as you go.

Follow Sifu Yik for daily AI tools, free resources, and content creation tips. Comment “FREE” below and get the full free business starter checklist.

5 AI PROMPTS TO MAKE YOU FAMOUS IN YOUR NICHE
Most people stay invisible for years.
These 5 prompts can change that this week.
Copy. Paste. Go.

## 1 / Define Your Unforgettable Brand
Prompt:
“Ask me 10 questions to uncover my unique strengths, values, and audience pain points. Then write me 3 bold personal positioning statements that make me impossible to ignore. Each one must be clear, specific, and different from everyone else in my niche.”

## 2 / Turn Your Skill Into a Content Plan
Prompt:
“Create a 30-day content calendar for [insert niche]. Give me 5 content formats I can rotate each week. Include a scroll-stopping hook for each format and one CTA that builds trust fast. Label every post by goal: awareness, trust, or action.”

## 3 / Build Authority From Zero
Prompt:
“I am starting from zero in [insert area]. Give me 5 specific strategies to build authority using only free content and social proof. No paid ads. No big following needed. Tell me exactly what to post, where to post it, and what to say to get people to see me as the go-to person.”

## 4 / Build Your Niche Network
Prompt:
“Create a 7-day plan to connect with 5 influential people in [insert niche] without being pushy or salesy. Give me 3 DM scripts for cold outreach, a value-first approach for every touchpoint, and a natural follow-up schedule that does not feel awkward.”

## 5 / Create Your Weekly Growth System
Prompt:
“Design a repeatable weekly content system for someone in [insert niche] who only has 1 to 2 hours a day. Tell me what to create, when to post, and how to turn one piece of content into 5 different formats. Make it simple enough to repeat every single week without burning out.”

## 💡 Pro Tips
- Always replace [brackets] with your real niche before using any prompt

- Run all 5 prompts in one chat session so AI builds on each answer

- Save all outputs in one doc and review every 30 days

- Treat your AI like a business partner, not just a search engine

- The more specific your answers, the better the output you will get

## ⚠️ The Truth
Most people never get known in their niche. Not because they lack talent. Because they never define who they are, who they serve, or what makes them different. These prompts fix all three in one sitting.

## 🚀 Quick Start
Open ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini right now. Paste Prompt 1. Answer every question honestly. You will have your brand positioning statement ready in under 5 minutes. That one step puts you ahead of 90% of people in your niche.

## 🎯 Bottom Line
You do not need a huge following to get known in your niche. You need a clear message, a consistent system, and the right prompts to guide you. Everything starts with one prompt today.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
