□ Choose 1 platform (master one before spreading)
□ Select 1 niche (fitness, finance, AI, beauty, business, etc.)
□ Identify 1 problem you'll solve
□ Write down: "I help [WHO] achieve [WHAT] without [PAIN POINT]"

DAY 2: STUDY THE WINNERS
□ Find 10 successful creators in your niche
□ Analyze their top 10 most viral posts
□ Note patterns: hooks, formats, posting times
□ Screenshot winning formats for reference

DAY 3: SET UP FOR SUCCESS
□ Optimize profile: Clear bio, professional photo, CTA link
□ Create content calendar template
□ Set up analytics tracking
□ Decide posting schedule (minimum: 1 post/day)

DAY 4: CREATE CONTENT BANK
□ Write 30 content ideas (1 per day)
□ Use formula: Education + Entertainment + Engagement
□ Batch create: Write 7 posts in one sitting
□ Have content ready before you need it

DAY 5: FIRST POST GOES LIVE
□ Post your first piece of content
□ Use a proven format from Day 2 research
□ Don't aim for perfection, aim for posted
□ Engage with 20 other creators in your niche

DAY 6: ENGAGEMENT BLITZ
□ Comment on 30 posts in your niche (meaningful comments)
□ Reply to every comment on your posts within 1 hour
□ Follow 20 accounts you can learn from
□ DM 5 creators with genuine compliments (no selling)

DAY 7: WEEKLY REVIEW
□ Check analytics: What worked? What flopped?
□ Double down on top-performing content type
□ Adjust strategy based on data
□ Plan Week 2 content

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📈 WEEK 2: GROWTH (Days 8-14)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

DAY 8: POST + ENGAGE
□ Post daily (stick to schedule)
□ Spend 30 min engaging before posting
□ Spend 30 min engaging after posting
□ Join 3 relevant groups/communities

DAY 9: SWIPE FILE BUILD
□ Create "viral hooks" swipe file (20+ hooks)
□ Test different hooks on same content
□ Track which hooks get most engagement
□ Save as templates

DAY 10: ADD VALUE BOMB
□ Post your most valuable content yet
□ Make it screenshot-worthy
□ Ask question at end to boost comments
□ Pin it to your profile

DAY 11: COLLABORATION DAY
□ DM 5 creators for collab/shoutout exchange
□ Engage heavily with their content
□ Look for win-win opportunities
□ Build genuine relationships

DAY 12: ANALYZE & ADAPT
□ Review analytics again
□ What time gets most engagement?
□ What format performs best?
□ Kill what doesn't work, 2x what does

DAY 13: CONTENT REMIX
□ Take your best post and remix it
□ Different format: Turn post into carousel/video/thread
□ Post on same platform or cross-promote
□ Reuse winning content in new ways

DAY 14: MILESTONE CHECK
□ Count followers gained (expect: 100-500 depending on platform)
□ Engagement rate improving?
□ Identify your "superfans" (people who engage regularly)
□ Thank them in DMs

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
💰 WEEK 3: MONETIZATION PREP (Days 15-21)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

DAY 15: CHOOSE MONEY METHOD
Pick 1 to start:
□ Affiliate marketing (easiest, fastest)
□ Digital product (ebook, template, checklist)
□ Service/coaching (highest pay per sale)
□ Sponsored posts (need bigger following)

DAY 16: BUILD YOUR OFFER
If Affiliate:
□ Join 3 affiliate programs in your niche
□ Pick 1 product you genuinely use/love
□ Get affiliate links ready

If Digital Product:
□ Outline simple guide/template/checklist
□ Solve one specific problem
□ Price: $7-27 to start

If Service:
□ Define service clearly
□ Set price: $97-497
□ Create simple sales page or pitch

DAY 17: CREATE LEAD MAGNET
□ Make free valuable resource
□ Solves mini-problem in your niche
□ Collect emails in exchange
□ Use Gumroad, Kit, or Google Form

DAY 18: SOFT SELL PRACTICE
□ Post valuable content with subtle CTA
□ "DM me [WORD] for [FREE THING]"
□ Test audience response
□ Start building email list

DAY 19: BUILD TRUST CONTENT
□ Share your story/journey
□ Show behind-the-scenes
□ Be vulnerable, be real
□ People buy from people they trust

DAY 20: TESTIMONIAL HUNT
□ If you've helped anyone before, ask for testimonial
□ Offer free value in exchange for case study
□ Screenshot positive comments/DMs
□ Social proof = sales fuel

DAY 21: SALES FUNNEL READY
□ Free content → Lead magnet → Email → Offer
□ Test entire flow yourself
□ Make sure all links work
□ You're ready to make money

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🎯 WEEK 4: FIRST DOLLAR (Days 22-30)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

DAY 22: SOFT LAUNCH
□ Post about your offer casually
□ Share the "why" behind creating it
□ Include clear CTA
□ Don't be salesy, be helpful

DAY 23: VALUE BOMB + CTA
□ Drop massive value
□ End with: "Want more? Link in bio" or "DM me [WORD]"
□ Follow up with everyone who engages
□ Conversations = conversions

DAY 24: URGENCY POST
□ Limited time offer or bonus
□ Create gentle FOMO
□ "Only helping 10 people this week"
□ Scarcity drives action

DAY 25: HANDLE OBJECTIONS
□ Post addressing common objections
□ "I thought [OBJECTION] too, until..."
□ Answer in comments/DMs
□ Make buying easy

DAY 26: SOCIAL PROOF SHARE
□ Post testimonials/results
□ Even if it's just one person
□ "This worked for them, it can work for you"
□ Proof > promises

DAY 27: LAST CALL
□ Final push post
□ Recap value + results
□ Clear CTA: "Link in bio" or "Comment [WORD]"
□ Follow up in DMs with everyone interested

DAY 28: CLOSE SALES
□ DM everyone who showed interest
□ Simple pitch: Problem → Solution → Price → CTA
□ Answer questions quickly
□ Close your first sale(s) 💰

DAY 29: DELIVER VALUE
□ Over-deliver on your promise
□ Blow their minds
□ Ask for testimonial/review
□ Happy customer = repeat customer + referrals

DAY 30: REFLECT & SCALE
□ Celebrate your first dollar! 🎉
□ Review what worked
□ Plan next 30 days: More of what works
□ Increase posting or add 2nd platform
□ Reinvest profit into growth

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔥 BONUS: DAILY NON-NEGOTIABLES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Every Single Day:
✅ Post 1 piece of valuable content
✅ Engage for 30 minutes (before you post)
✅ Reply to ALL comments within 1 hour
✅ DM 3-5 new people (genuine connection)
✅ Study 1 viral post in your niche
✅ Track analytics
✅ Move 1 follower closer to buying

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
💡 SUCCESS FORMULAS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

VIRAL POST FORMULA:
Hook (1 line) → Value (3-5 points) → CTA (comment/save/follow)

ENGAGEMENT FORMULA:
Give 10x before you ask 1x

MONETIZATION FORMULA:
Audience + Trust + Offer + CTA = Money

GROWTH FORMULA:
Consistency + Value + Engagement = Followers

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

❌ Posting without engaging first
❌ Spreading across too many platforms
❌ Waiting for "perfect" content
❌ Ignoring analytics
❌ Selling before building trust
❌ Giving up before Day 30
❌ Copying without adding your unique angle
❌ Focusing on followers instead of buyers

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
✅ QUICK WINS CHECKLIST
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

□ Profile optimized for conversions
□ 30 posts published
□ 100+ engaged followers
□ Lead magnet created
□ First offer launched
□ First dollar earned
□ Email list started
□ Content system established
□ Analytics reviewed weekly
□ Momentum building

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 YOUR ONLY JOB: Execute this plan for 30 days. No excuses. No skipping. No "I'll start Monday."

The ones who follow this blueprint make money.
The ones who don't stay broke.

Choose wisely.

Now GO. 🚀

💰 20 100% FREE Tools To Start Your Small Business (No Credit Card, No Hidden Fees!)

I tested every single one. Here's what actually works:

✅ 1. X (TWITTER) - Brand Building
Features:
- Free business profile
- Unlimited posts
- Brand visibility
- Engagement tools
- Analytics dashboard
- No ads required
URL: https://x.com

✅ 2. CANVA - Graphic Design
Features:
- 250,000+ free templates
- Drag-and-drop editor
- Social media graphics
- Logo design tools
- Photo editing
- Free forever plan
URL: https://canva.com

✅ 3. WIX - Website Builder
Features:
- 50+ free templates
- Mobile responsive design
- Free hosting included
- No coding required
- SSL security
- 500MB storage
URL: https://wix.com

✅ 4. BREVO (SENDINBLUE) - Email Marketing
Features:
- 9,000 emails per month
- 100,000 contacts limit
- Email automation
- Landing pages
- SMS campaigns
- Real-time analytics
URL: https://brevo.com

✅ 5. CHATGPT - AI Content Writer
Features:
- Unlimited conversations
- Blog post writing
- Social media captions
- Product descriptions
- Email copy
- 24/7 availability
URL: https://chat.openai.com

✅ 6. HUBSPOT SERVICE HUB - Customer Support
Features:
- Free ticketing system
- Live chat widget
- Shared team inbox
- Knowledge base builder
- Conversation routing
- Team collaboration
URL: https://hubspot.com/products/service

✅ 7. KO-FI - Online Store
Features:
- Sell digital products
- 0% fees on donations
- 5% fee on sales (still lowest)
- Memberships & commissions
- No monthly subscription
- Instant PayPal/Stripe payouts
URL: https://ko-fi.com

✅ 8. ZOHO INVOICE - Invoicing
Features:
- Unlimited invoices forever
- Professional templates
- Payment tracking
- Expense management
- Client portal access
- Multi-currency support
URL: https://zoho.com/invoice

✅ 9. TRELLO - Project Management
Features:
- Unlimited cards
- 10 boards per workspace
- File attachments
- Checklists & due dates
- Mobile app
- Team collaboration
URL: https://trello.com

✅ 10. N8N - Workflow Automation
Features:
- Self-hosted = 100% free
- 200+ app integrations
- Visual workflow builder
- Unlimited workflows
- No task limits ever
- Open source
URL: https://n8n.io

✅ 11. GNUCASH - Accounting Software
Features:
- Double-entry accounting
- Income/expense tracking
- Invoice generation
- Financial reports
- Tax preparation tools
- Forever free, no limits
URL: https://gnucash.org

✅ 12. HUBSPOT CRM - Customer Relationship Management
Features:
- Up to 1,000,000 contacts
- Deal pipeline tracking
- Email tracking & templates
- Meeting scheduler
- Reporting dashboard
- 100% free forever
URL: https://hubspot.com/products/crm

✅ 13. TOGGL TRACK - Time Tracking
Features:
- Up to 5 team members
- Unlimited time entries
- Detailed reporting
- Project tracking
- Mobile & desktop apps
- One-click timers
URL: https://toggl.com/track

✅ 14. GOOGLE DRIVE - Cloud Storage
Features:
- 15GB free storage
- Real-time collaboration
- File sharing controls
- Access from anywhere
- Automatic backup
- Version history
URL: https://drive.google.com

✅ 15. NOTION - All-in-One Workspace
Features:
- Unlimited pages & blocks
- Wikis & documentation
- Task management
- Databases & tables
- 1,000+ free templates
- Team collaboration
URL: https://notion.so

✅ 16. TALLY FORMS - Form Builder
Features:
- Unlimited forms
- Unlimited submissions
- No Tally branding
- Conditional logic
- File uploads (10MB)
- Notion & Airtable sync
URL: https://tally.so

✅ 17. NAMELIX - AI Logo Generator
Features:
- AI-powered designs
- Customizable logos
- Multiple style options
- Filter by industry
- Brand name suggestions
- Instant generation
URL: https://namelix.com

✅ 18. SUBSTACK - Newsletter Platform
Features:
- Free publishing forever
- Email newsletter system
- Custom domain support
- Built-in subscriber management
- Simple monetization (10% fee)
- No upfront costs
URL: https://substack.com

✅ 19. NOTEBOOKLM - AI Presentation Maker
Features:
- AI-powered slide decks
- Document analysis
- Audio overviews
- Automatic citations
- Up to 100 notebooks free
- Source-grounded outputs
URL: https://notebooklm.google.com

✅ 20. GOOGLE ANALYTICS - Website Analytics
Features:
- Website traffic tracking
- User behavior analysis
- Real-time reporting
- Conversion tracking
- Audience insights
- Free for most businesses
URL: https://analytics.google.com

---

💡 PRO TIPS:
→ Start with #1, 2, 3, 5 (brand, design, website, content) - build your foundation first
→ Add email marketing (#4) once you hit 50+ daily visitors
→ Use n8n (#10) to automate repetitive tasks between tools - saves 10+ hours weekly
→ Most tools stay free forever for small businesses under 10K visitors/month
→ Export your data monthly as backup - always control your assets

🔍 THE TRUTH:
I've run my VA company (30+ staff) on this exact stack for 24 months. Total software cost? $0. The real cost? Your time learning each tool. Ko-fi charges 5% on sales but 0% on donations - still better than Gumroad's 10%. Substack takes 10% only when you monetize. n8n requires self-hosting but gives you unlimited automation. These aren't "free trials" - they're genuinely free tiers designed for small businesses.

⚡ QUICK START (8-Hour Day 1 Blueprint):
• Hour 1: Create X account + Generate logo on Namelix
• Hour 2: Design 5 posts on Canva + schedule
• Hour 3: Build 5-page Wix website (use template)
• Hour 4: Set up Google Analytics tracking code
• Hour 5: Create HubSpot CRM + import contacts
• Hour 6: Write first newsletter on Substack
• Hour 7: Set up Brevo email capture form
• Hour 8: Post on X + engage 10 accounts

🎯 BOTTOM LINE:
$0 in software. 30 days of daily execution. That's the real formula. I've coached 50+ people who built $3K-$10K/month businesses using only these tools. The "I need money to start" excuse is dead. Tally gives you unlimited form submissions. HubSpot gives you 1M free contacts. Brevo sends 9,000 emails monthly. You're not limited by tools - you're limited by action.

Start with one niche, not five. Pick a topic you can talk about for 90 days without getting bored. Make every post short, useful, and easy to save or share.

Evergreen niches work because people always need help with daily life, habits, work, learning, and growth. You do not need to be an expert, but you do need to be clear and consistent.

Choose one niche today, write 10 simple post ideas, and test them this week. Use short hooks, easy English, and practical tips your audience can use right away.

The best niche is not the most trendy one. The best niche is the one you can explain clearly, post about often, and keep improving over time

Create a personalized financial plan covering budgeting, emergency savings, debt management, investing, taxes, retirement planning, insurance considerations, and long-term wealth building.”
Why it works: This turns Claude into one advisor who sees your whole financial picture, not just one piece of it. Most people fix budgeting but ignore insurance or taxes. This prompt forces a full system, not a patch job.
2. The Leaky Bucket Budget Fix Prompt
“Act as an elite budgeting consultant. Analyze my monthly income and spending habits to build a budget that aligns with my financial goals. Categorize expenses, identify unnecessary spending, recommend realistic savings targets, and create spending rules that are easy to maintain. Include weekly and monthly review systems.”
Why it works: Most budgets fail because they are too strict or too vague. This prompt asks for rules you can actually keep, plus built in review checkpoints so the plan does not die after week one.
3. The Compounding Wealth Path Prompt
“Act as a long-term wealth strategist. Create a step-by-step roadmap for building wealth based on my income, age, financial goals, and investment timeline. Cover emergency funds, investing principles, retirement accounts (where applicable), diversified investing concepts, compounding, and risk management. Explain the reasoning behind each recommendation.”
Why it works: Wealth building fails when people copy advice that does not fit their age or timeline. This prompt personalizes the roadmap and explains the “why” behind every step so you actually understand your own plan.
4. The Debt Freedom Fast Track Prompt
“Act as a financial coach specializing in debt management. Analyze my debts and create the most efficient repayment strategy based on interest rates, balances, cash flow, and financial goals. Compare repayment methods, explain trade offs, and build a realistic repayment schedule while maintaining healthy savings habits.”
Why it works: Snowball vs avalanche method confuses most people. This prompt makes Claude compare both, pick what fits your cash flow, and still protect your savings while you pay off debt.
5. The Set It and Forget It Money System Prompt
“Act as a personal finance systems designer. Build an automated financial management system that simplifies budgeting, saving, investing, bill payments, subscriptions, and financial tracking. Recommend automation strategies, review schedules, alerts, dashboards, and organizational methods that reduce manual work while maintaining oversight.”
Why it works: Discipline fades, systems do not. This prompt shifts the work from willpower to automation so your money manages itself even on your busy weeks.
6. The Income Ceiling Breaker Prompt
“Act as a career and financial strategist. Analyze my current earning potential and recommend realistic ways to increase my income over the next 12 to 36 months. Include career advancement, skill development, side businesses, freelance opportunities, digital products, investments, and other income sources. Rank recommendations by effort, risk, startup cost, and long term earning potential.”
Why it works: Budgeting only gets you so far. This prompt attacks the other side of the equation, your income, and ranks every option so you know what to try first based on your effort and risk level.
7. The Smarter Money Moves Checklist Prompt
“Act as a financial decision making advisor. Build a framework that helps me make smarter financial decisions involving major purchases, investments, loans, subscriptions, insurance, and lifestyle choices. Create checklists, risk assessments, opportunity cost analyses, and decision trees that improve financial judgment over time.”
Why it works: Most bad money decisions happen in the moment. This prompt gives you a repeatable checklist so you slow down and think clearly before every big purchase or commitment.
8. The Decade of Freedom Roadmap Prompt
“Act as a professional financial planner. Create a detailed 10 year roadmap for improving my financial position. Include yearly milestones for savings, investments, debt reduction, income growth, emergency reserves, major purchases, retirement preparation, and financial independence. Build measurable KPIs and annual review systems to keep the plan adaptable as my life changes.”
Why it works: A 10 year view stops you from panicking over slow months. This prompt breaks a huge goal into yearly checkpoints with real numbers to track, so progress feels visible instead of invisible.
💡 Pro Tips
Give Claude real numbers, not vague guesses. The more detail you feed in, the sharper the plan.
Run these prompts every 3 to 6 months. Your income and goals change, your plan should too.
Stack prompts. Use the Budget Fix first, then the Debt Fast Track, then the Wealth Path.
🎯 The Truth
A financial plan means nothing if you do not review it. These prompts build the plan, you still have to check in monthly and adjust. AI gives you the map, you still have to walk the road.
⚡ Quick Start
Copy prompt 1. Paste it into Claude. Add your real income, expenses and goals. Read the full plan. Pick one action to start this week.
🔑 Bottom Line
You do not need a financial advisor to get a real plan. You need the right prompts and 20 minutes. Save this post before it disappears from your feed.

other_posts.text:
THE STRONGER YOU ACT, THE STRONGER YOU BECOME.
Growing up, we thought “faking it” was fake.
Turns out, almost every strong person you admire faked it first.
Not to impress anyone.
To train themselves into the person they wanted to become.
Here are 4 things strong people fake, on purpose, every single day.
- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

1. THEY ACT LIKE THEY DIDN’T HEAR IT
Not every insult deserves a reply.
What people think of you is their business, not yours.
Mature people stop explaining themselves.
Results always speak louder than arguments ever will.
2. THEY ACT LIKE THEY DIDN’T SEE IT
Not every drama needs your presence.
Not everyone deserves your energy.
The realest kind of growing up is learning to walk away from people and situations that drain you.
Sometimes you see it clearly, and you still choose to let it go.
Not because you lost. Because it was never worth winning.
3. THEY ACT LIKE IT DOESN’T HURT
Everyone gets disappointed. Everyone gets hurt.
Strong people aren’t emotionless.
They just wipe their eyes and keep showing up for the day ahead.
Because emotions don’t fix anything. Action does.
4. THEY ACT LIKE THEY’RE ALREADY WORKING HARD, EVEN WHEN NO ONE IS WATCHING
No audience. Still showing up.
No applause. Still moving forward.
People think you were just born talented.
What they never see are the quiet, unglamorous days that actually changed your life.
🎯 PRO TIPS
Pick ONE of these four and practice it for 7 days straight. Don’t try all four at once, that’s how people quit by day 2.
💡 THE TRUTH
Nobody is naturally this calm or this disciplined. Every strong person you know built it through repetition, not personality.
🚀 QUICK START
Tonight, write down one thing you usually react to (a comment, a rumor, a bad mood) and practice “acting like you didn’t” tomorrow morning.
📌 BOTTOM LINE
Confidence isn’t something you wait to feel. It’s something you act into existence, one small moment at a time.
Comment “STRONG” and I’ll send you the full breakdown with examples for each of the 4 points.

other_posts.title: 15 Mindset Shifts That Separate Rich People From Everyone Else
other_posts.text:
15 Mindset Shifts That Separate Rich People From Everyone Else
Have you noticed how two people can start at the exact same point, and years later, one is thriving while the other is stuck?
I spent months studying people who built real wealth and comparing them to people who work just as hard but stay stuck. The gap was never about effort. It was mindset.
These 15 shifts come from wealth psychology research, interviews, and pattern watching. Some of these might sting. But knowing them early can save you years of struggle.
- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

1. TIME
Poor mindset: Time is free, save it whenever you can
Rich mindset: Time is the most valuable asset, spend money to protect it
Someone skips a short ride to save a little cash and loses an hour of their day instead. That hour was worth more than what they saved.
2. SPENDING ORDER
Poor mindset: Get paid, spend first, treat yourself
Rich mindset: Get paid, invest first, spend what is left
It is not about never enjoying your money. It is about sequence. Sequence decides your future.
3. RISK
Poor mindset: Chase safety, fear every risk
Rich mindset: Calculate the risk, take it if it is manageable
Wealthy people are not gamblers. They run the numbers and always have a backup plan. Poor mindset avoids trying at all because failing feels too scary.
4. LEARNING
Poor mindset: Learn just enough to get by
Rich mindset: Never stop learning, your mind is your biggest lever
Every wealthy person I have studied still learns daily. Many invest more into their own growth every year than most people spend on basic living costs.
5. YOUR CIRCLE
Poor mindset: Hang out with whoever feels comfortable
Rich mindset: Get closer to people who are ahead of you
Your habits and income tend to match the people you spend the most time with. Old saying, still true.
6. PROBLEMS
Poor mindset: A problem is bad news, avoid it
Rich mindset: A problem is an opportunity, solve it and get paid
Every frustration hides a business idea. It depends on how you look at it.
7. GOALS
Poor mindset: Wants more money but has no clear number
Rich mindset: Sets a specific target with a real deadline
Saying I want to be rich and saying I want to hit a specific savings goal in three years send completely different signals to your brain.
8. FAILURE
Poor mindset: I failed means I am not capable
Rich mindset: I failed means I just eliminated one wrong path
Most successful founders failed many times before it worked. Every failure was tuition, not proof of weakness.
9. FOCUS
Poor mindset: Chase whatever trend is making noise
Rich mindset: Go deep in one lane and stay patient
Jumping from trend to trend leaves you with nothing built. Staying focused compounds.
10. NETWORKING
Poor mindset: Feels embarrassed to ask for help
Rich mindset: Offers value first, builds relationships that go both ways
Real networking is not about who can help you. It is about why anyone would want to help you at all. The answer is you bring value too.
11. PASSIVE INCOME
Poor mindset: Income only comes from active work
Rich mindset: Build systems that keep earning while you sleep
This is why wealthy people get freer as they grow, while others get busier and more stuck. This one point changes everything.
12. EMOTIONS
Poor mindset: Emotional decisions, impulse buys
Rich mindset: Data first, delay the reward
Before buying anything, ask yourself if it is a want or a need. Wait a full day before deciding.
13. OPPORTUNITY
Poor mindset: Wait for luck to show up
Rich mindset: Create the opening yourself, solving problems is the opportunity
Opportunity is never handed to you. You build it step by step.
14. INFORMATION
Poor mindset: Scrolls short videos for information
Rich mindset: Pays for quality information, builds a personal knowledge source
Information gaps create wealth gaps. What you are shown for free is usually what someone else wants you to see.
15. LONG TERM THINKING
Poor mindset: Lives for right now, wants instant results
Rich mindset: Delays gratification, trusts compounding
Wealth is built from time plus compounding. Every choice you make today shapes who you are three years from now.
Here is the hard truth. Poor mindset does not come from being poor. Having that mindset is often what keeps someone poor.
Good news, mindset can be rebuilt. Start today. Pick three of these and practice on purpose. Check back in three months and thank yourself.
✅ PRO TIPS
Pick your weakest three mindsets first. Fixing your biggest leaks always beats trying to fix all fifteen at once.
🔥 THE TRUTH
None of this is about luck or talent. It is about which patterns you repeat every single day without noticing.
🚀 QUICK START
Day 1, pick your three weak points
Day 2, write one small action for each
Day 7, review what changed
Day 30, replace old habits with new defaults
💡 BOTTOM LINE
Mindset shifts are free, but the results are not. Start small, stay consistent, and let time do the compounding for you.

other_posts.title: 10 Habits That Keep People Broke Forever
other_posts.text:
# 10 Habits That Keep People Broke Forever
- -

Let’s break them down. I’m grouping these 10 patterns into 4 categories: Trust, Action, Courage, and Relationships.
1️⃣ They Chase quick cash only
Small money is visible. Trust (the real asset) is invisible. This is the most dangerous trap of all.
2️⃣ They Take promises lightly
“I’ll call you back.” “Let’s do this next time.” Every broken promise quietly drains your trust account.
3️⃣ They Underestimate trust
Trust can’t be seen. That’s exactly why people ignore it. But trust is what pulls money toward you, every single time.
4️⃣ They barely take action
Steve Jobs got rejected by investors dozens of times before Apple took off. He kept knocking. Success isn’t luck, it’s reps.
5️⃣ They avoid risk out of fear
When Sara Blakely started Spanx, everyone told her it would fail. She had zero background in fashion. She did it anyway.
6️⃣ They never go deep on what they love
Steve Jobs didn’t just sell computers, he obsessed over design, fonts, and user experience like a fan, not a founder.
7️⃣ They treat people like tools
Treat people like stepping stones, and connections vanish. Real relationships only come back to those who give first.
8️⃣ They are sloppy with small tasks
Small jobs are the smallest unit of trust. Mess these up, and bigger opportunities will never find you.
9️⃣ They envy successful people
Every minute spent jealous is a minute not spent building. Winners study success. Losers resent it.
🔟 They wait for the “right moment”
Opportunity does not wait around. It shows up for people who already moved, like someone who kept showing up at doors that kept closing.
Look closely, and one line connects all 10.
Every single one comes down to this: are you building trust, or chasing quick wins?

## 🏦 So How Do You Actually Build Trust?
Think of trust like a piggy bank.
You cannot dump a fortune in at once. You drop in one coin at a time, over and over.
Keep a promise, that’s one coin.
Do a small job well, another coin.
Get rejected and show up again anyway, another coin.
Do it 3 times, barely noticeable.
Do it 10 times, people start to notice.
Do it 30 times, opportunities start finding you.
Trust isn’t built with willpower. It’s built with repetition.
One “guaranteed quick win,” on the other hand, can empty that piggy bank instantly. I know because it happened to me.

## WHAT TO DO TOMORROW
Do not try to fix all 10 today. That’s how people quit on day two.
Fix just one thing first: stop chasing quick wins, and stop rushing the small task in front of you.
Think of the one task on your plate right now that feels the most “not worth my time.”
Tomorrow, do that one task slightly better than usual.
That’s it. That one task is your first coin in the piggy bank.

## ✅ Pro Tips
- Track every promise you make this week. Keep 100% of them, even the small ones.

- Pick the task you’re most tempted to rush through, and do it slower, better, cleaner.

- Follow up with someone you got rejected by. Rejection isn’t the end, it’s round one.

- Study one successful person you envy. Turn jealousy into a lesson.

- Say no to any offer that sounds “too easy.” Real trust takes time, always.

## 🔍 The Truth
None of these 10 habits are about intelligence or luck. They’re about direction. Every single day, you’re choosing between two paths: building trust slowly, or chasing shortcuts fast. Shortcuts feel good for a moment, but they empty the account. Trust feels slow, but it compounds. The people who “make it” aren’t smarter. They just made this choice correctly, over and over, longer than everyone else.

## 🚀 Quick Start
- Pick ONE small task you’ve been avoiding or rushing.

- Do it tomorrow with full effort, no shortcuts.

- Keep one promise you almost broke this week.

- Reach out to one person you got rejected by before.

- Write down one thing you’re jealous of, then turn it into a goal.

## 💡 Bottom Line
Don’t try to fix all 10 habits overnight, you’ll burn out and quit. Pick ONE small task you’ve been treating as “not worth it,” and do it right tomorrow. That’s your first coin in the piggy bank. Everything else builds from there.

other_posts.title: 5 AI PROMPTS Every PhD Student Needs
other_posts.text:
- -

5 AI PROMPTS Every PhD Student Needs
(copy-paste templates )
If you’re still typing “summarize this paper” into ChatGPT, you’re leaving 80% of the value on the table.

- -

—
01. THE SOURCE CONNECTOR
For when you have 15 tabs open and no idea how the papers relate.
Copy paste prompt:
“I’m writing a literature review on [YOUR TOPIC]. I’ll give you summaries of several papers one at a time. After each one, don’t just summarize, tell me how it agrees, disagrees, or adds a new angle compared to the papers I’ve already given you. At the end, help me group them into 2 to 3 themes I can use as subheadings.”
Why it works: You are forcing the model to compare, not repeat. Comparison is the actual academic skill a literature review is supposed to show, so this prompt trains the output toward synthesis instead of summary.
—
02. THE BLIND SPOT HUNTER
This is the one that saves you months. Every supervisor asks “what’s the gap” and every student freezes.
Copy paste prompt:
“Based on these papers on [YOUR TOPIC], act as a critical reviewer. List what has been studied extensively, what has been studied but with conflicting results, and what hasn’t been studied at all. Then suggest 3 possible research questions that address an actual gap, not just a variation of existing work.”
Why it works: Gap finding is a comparison task across many sources at once, something the human brain struggles to hold in memory but AI handles easily. Naming the gap this clearly also gives you a ready answer the moment your supervisor asks.
—
03. THE COMMITTEE SIMULATOR
Before you defend your methodology to your committee, defend it to AI first.
Copy paste prompt:
“Here is my proposed research methodology: [PASTE METHODOLOGY]. Play the role of a strict thesis committee member. Identify any weaknesses in sample size, validity, bias, or method choice. Ask me the 3 toughest questions a reviewer might ask about this methodology.”
Why it works: Role play prompts push AI to adopt a critical stance instead of a supportive one, which surfaces weaknesses you would otherwise only discover during the real defense.
—
04. THE FORMAL VOICE FIXER
For when you know what you want to say, but it comes out sounding like a text message instead of a thesis.
Copy paste prompt:
“Rewrite the following paragraph in formal academic tone suitable for a peer reviewed journal in [YOUR FIELD]. Keep all the original meaning and citations, but improve sentence structure, remove casual language, and ensure it reads as objective and precise: [PASTE YOUR PARAGRAPH]”
Why it works: This isolates tone and structure from content, so the AI is polishing your ideas rather than inventing new ones. That keeps your original argument intact while fixing the delivery.
—
05. THE EXAMINER ROLEPLAY
The one you wish existed when you were defending my own PhD.
Copy paste prompt:
“I’m preparing for my PhD viva or defense. My thesis is about [ONE LINE SUMMARY]. Act as an external examiner. Ask me 5 questions ranging from easy to very difficult, covering my methodology, my contribution to the field, and potential weaknesses. After each answer I give you, tell me honestly if a real examiner would accept it or push further.”
Why it works: Live back and forth simulation trains your recall under pressure, which is closer to how a real viva feels than reading prepared answers off a page.
📌 PRO TIPS
• Feed AI your own draft first, never let it write content it hasn’t seen from you
• Push back when an answer feels generic, ask it to get specific to your field
• Do the viva prompt out loud, not just typed, treat it like a real rehearsal
• Run the methodology prompt before you submit your proposal, not after
• Always fact check anything AI generates, never let it invent citations
• Save every good AI conversation as a reusable template for your next chapter
🔍 THE TRUTH
AI will not write your thesis for you, and it should not. What it actually does well is speed up the thinking work around your thesis: spotting patterns across papers, stress testing your logic, and cleaning up your language so your ideas land clearly. The students getting real value from these tools are not asking AI to think for them, they are using it as a sparring partner that pushes back. Treat it like a smart but overconfident research assistant who needs fact checking, and it becomes genuinely useful.
🚀 QUICK START
• Pick one prompt above that matches what you are stuck on right now
• Copy it exactly, then fill in your topic or paste your own text
• Run it in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, results vary slightly between tools
• Read the output critically, do not accept the first answer as final
• Ask a follow up question to push the AI deeper before you move on
• Save the prompt somewhere you will actually find it again next week
🎯 BOTTOM LINE
These prompts will not replace your thinking, but they will remove the friction that keeps you stuck for hours. Use them as a starting point, not a finish line, and your thesis moves faster with less stress.
DON’T JUST SCROLL.
USE THESE.
Save this post, screenshot the 5 prompts, and actually use them this week - not just watch and forget.

## ✅ PRO TIPS
- Batch your hooks. Write 10 in one sitting so you never run out.

- Use the first 2 seconds to ask a question or make a bold claim.

- Keep captions short. Long captions kill watch time.

- Reuse your best performing format with a new topic.

- Add on-screen text. Many people watch with the sound off.

- End every reel with one clear next step, like a comment prompt.

- Study your top 3 reels and repeat what worked.

- Post consistently instead of waiting for the perfect idea.

- Repost old ideas with a fresh hook. Most people never saw it the first time.

- Keep one reel per idea. Do not overload a single video with too much info.

## 🎯 THE TRUTH
There is no secret trick to going viral. Growth comes from testing hooks, showing up consistently, and giving real value people can use right away. Most creators do not fail because they run out of ideas. They fail because they stop posting too soon or try to make everything perfect before sharing it. The algorithm rewards watch time, so a strong hook gets attention, but a real answer or story is what keeps people watching until the end. Simple, honest content beats overproduced content almost every time.

## 🏁 QUICK START

- Match each hook to one tip, lesson, or story you already know.

- Film all 5 in one sitting to save time and stay consistent.

- Add on-screen captions and one simple call to action.

- Post one reel per day for 5 days and track the results.

- Take your best performing reel and repeat the format with a new topic.

## 📌 BOTTOM LINE
🔑 You do not need 200 brand new ideas every single week. You need a handful of strong hooks and the discipline to post them consistently. Pick one idea from this list right now, make it yours, and hit post today.

other_posts.title: 7 Claude Prompt that Build You A Premium Website
other_posts.text:
- -

🚨 BREAKING: Claude can now make your website look like a real design studio built it. Not a template. Not that “obvious AI” look everyone spots now.
Most people still use lazy prompts. That’s why they end up with generic layouts, the same purple gradient everyone else has, and default fonts that scream “I used a builder.”
Use these 7 prompts instead. Save this post. You’ll want it later. 🔖
- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

1. The Signature Blueprint Prompt
“Act as a senior website strategist and UX architect. I want a website for [business type] that feels intentionally designed and custom built, not assembled from a template. First, ask me up to 5 sharp clarifying questions about my brand personality, audience, offer, and visual style. Then give me: the exact page structure a polished site should use, which sections most template sites skip, the layout decisions that create a premium feel, what belongs above the fold, and the ONE mistake that instantly makes a DIY site look cheap.”
Why it works: Making Claude ask questions first stops it from guessing your brand and defaulting to the safest, most generic answer. Studies show users form trust judgments about websites in as little as 50 milliseconds, before they’ve read a single word, and that snap judgment is almost entirely emotional and aesthetic. Context up front is what closes that gap.
2. The Anti Sameness Type Prompt
“Act as a typography director. My site currently uses [describe fonts]. Give me: a font pairing that feels intentional instead of default, a full type scale for headings, subheadings, body text and buttons, the right line height and letter spacing for each, and the ONE typography habit that makes even good content look amateur.”
Why it works: Default fonts are one of the biggest giveaways of a low effort site. Research on AI generated design notes that seeing a default typeface paired with no other typographic choices is a strong signal the design was never intentionally styled. Asking for an actual scale, not just “make it nicer,” gives you numbers you can use immediately.
3. The Breathing Room Auditor
“Act as a layout critic reviewing my page: [upload screenshots]. Go section by section. Tell me: where it feels cramped, where it feels empty in the wrong way, the exact spacing changes that would make it feel more expensive, and why generous white space is one of the fastest signals of a premium build.”
Why it works: This isn’t a vague feeling. White space creates visual breathing room that improves readability, guides attention, and communicates sophistication, and strategic use increases content comprehension by 20 percent. Uploading real screenshots means the feedback is about your actual page, not generic theory.
4. The Purposeful Motion Prompt
“Act as an interaction designer. My site is mostly static. Give me 3 small hover or scroll interactions that add polish without needing custom animation work. For each, tell me exactly where it belongs, what triggers it, and why it improves perceived quality. Then tell me the line between a tasteful detail and a distracting gimmick.”
Why it works: Overdone motion is a dead giveaway of an AI build. One design breakdown points out that everything fading in, everything glowing on hover, and everything having a subtle transform when it enters the viewport is a common AI pattern, because AI generated sites often mistake motion for polish. This prompt keeps you on the tasteful side of that line.
5. The Case Study Framer
“Act as a presentation specialist. I want my work section to look like a design studio’s case study page. Give me: the structure for presenting one project persuasively, exactly what to show versus leave out, how much text to use, and a caption style that lets the work speak for itself.”
Why it works: Amateur portfolios dump every asset on the page. Studios curate and tell a story instead. This prompt forces Claude to think like an editor cutting things out, which is the actual skill that separates a case study from a gallery.
6. The Trust Signal Sweep
“Act as a pre launch reviewer trained to spot amateur tells. Here is my site description: [describe]. Give me: the 5 small details that separate polished from unfinished, the order to fix them in, and the ONE thing worth obsessing over even if everything else is done. Also flag anything that looks like a fake or generic trust signal instead of a real one.”
Why it works: Fake trust elements are one of the most damaging AI tells. One analysis found that AI built sites often include the structural elements of trustworthy sites like testimonials and certificates without real substance behind them. This prompt catches that before you publish, not after.
7. The Reference Anchor Prompt (bonus, most people skip this one)
“Anchor my site’s visual direction to this reference: [paste a screenshot or link of a site you admire]. Match its type scale, spacing rhythm, and how it uses a single accent color, but do not copy it. Write real, specific copy for MY business, not filler lines. Tell me what you changed and why.”
Why it works: Vague requests get you the statistical average of every design Claude has seen. Design critics have flagged that AI generated layouts look familiar because they are statistically normal, and visual hierarchies technically function but feel like they were made for no one in particular. Feeding in a real reference is the single fastest way to break out of that average.

📌 Pro Tips
- Never let Claude design, write copy, and code all in one prompt. Split it into taste first, structure second, code last.

- Always paste a real reference image or link before asking for a redesign. Describing a vibe from memory keeps you stuck at “average.”

- Ask for exact numbers (font sizes, spacing values, hex codes) instead of vague words like “modern” or “clean.”

- Replace every placeholder image with a real photo or screenshot. Generic stock visuals are one of the fastest ways a site loses trust.

- Run the Trust Signal Sweep before every single publish, not just once. Treat it as a habit, not a one time step.

- Keep motion to one deliberate detail per section. If everything moves, nothing feels special.

🕵️ The Truth
A site doesn’t look premium because it cost a lot. It looks premium because someone made deliberate choices and left things out on purpose. The result of skipping this is design averaging, where layouts feel familiar because they’re statistically normal, and visitors can’t always articulate it, but they feel the absence of a real point of view. Claude can absolutely get you to studio quality, but only if you feed it real references, tight constraints, and a critic’s eye instead of a vague “make it look nice” request. The tool isn’t the bottleneck. The decisions you feed into it are.
🚀 Quick Start
- Screenshot your current homepage.

- Pick ONE prompt above that matches your weakest area: structure, type, spacing, motion, portfolio, trust, or reference.

- Paste a screenshot or reference link into the prompt.

- Apply ONE fix at a time. Don’t run all 7 prompts in one sitting.

- Run the Trust Signal Sweep right before you hit publish.

🎯 Bottom Line
You don’t need a big studio budget to get a studio quality feeling site. You need the right questions in the right order, real references instead of vague vibes, and the discipline to leave things out. Claude can carry the weight. The taste still has to come from you.

## Category 1 - Online Directories

## 1. Google Maps

## Why This Works
Most local businesses rely on Google Maps for calls, directions, and enquiries, but many profiles are under-optimized and lose visibility because basic details are incomplete or outdated.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Dentists

- Salons

- Gyms

- Clinics

- Restaurants

- Local service businesses

## What To Look For
- Fewer reviews than top competitors

- No recent photos

- Unanswered reviews

- Missing services or business details

- No updates or posts

## How To Find Leads
Search terms like:
- dentist near me

- salon in Austin

- gym in Manchester

- chiropractor in Toronto

Open the top listings and note obvious gaps.

## Outreach Example
“Hi, I came across your business while searching in your area and noticed a few opportunities that could improve visibility and enquiries. Happy to share them.”

## Pro Tip
Do not lead with your service. Lead with the opportunity you found.

## Common Mistake
Sending a generic marketing pitch without showing specific proof.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐ Easy
- -

## 2. Yelp

## Why This Works
Businesses on Yelp already understand online visibility and reputation management, which means they are more likely to value help that improves conversion and trust.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Restaurants

- Home services

- Beauty businesses

- Healthcare clinics

- Local retail businesses

## What To Look For
- Incomplete profile

- Weak or outdated photos

- Unanswered reviews

- Low review volume compared to competitors

- No clear website or booking path

## How To Find Leads
Search by category and city, then compare their Yelp profile with their website and social channels.

## Outreach Example
“I found your Yelp profile and noticed customers are discovering you there, but there are a few gaps that may be costing you enquiries after that first visit.”

## Pro Tip
Show where attention is being lost between discovery and action.

## Common Mistake
Pitching reputation management without proving the missed opportunity.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐ Easy
- -

## 3. Thumbtack

## Why This Works
Many service professionals use lead platforms to get work but have not built a strong brand outside the platform.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Photographers

- Tutors

- Event planners

- Home service providers

- Consultants

## What To Look For
- Weak website

- No consistent branding

- Minimal reviews outside the platform

- No portfolio or case studies

## How To Find Leads
Look for providers who have been active for a while but still depend heavily on platform visibility.

## Outreach Example
“I noticed you’re getting discovered through Thumbtack. Have you considered building a stronger direct presence so you’re less dependent on one platform?”

## Pro Tip
Position your offer around ownership, not just promotion.

## Common Mistake
Trying to sell before understanding how they currently get clients.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐ Easy
- -

## 4. Clutch

## Why This Works
Agencies and B2B service companies on Clutch care about positioning, credibility, and lead generation, but many still have weak thought leadership and content.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Agencies

- Development firms

- Marketing consultancies

- B2B service providers

## What To Look For
- Weak LinkedIn activity

- No case studies beyond directory listings

- Outdated website

- Poor messaging or unclear positioning

## How To Find Leads
Search by service category and shortlist firms with strong services but weak digital presentation.

## Outreach Example
“I came across your Clutch listing and noticed your credibility is strong, but there may be a few missed opportunities in how your expertise is being presented online.”

## Pro Tip
B2B companies care more about trust and qualified leads than vanity metrics.

## Common Mistake
Talking about engagement when they care about pipeline.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐⭐ Medium
- -

## 5. GoodFirms

## Why This Works
Many companies listed on GoodFirms compete in crowded categories, so stronger positioning can help them stand out beyond price.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Software firms

- Marketing agencies

- IT consultancies

- Product development teams

## What To Look For
- Generic website copy

- No clear differentiation

- Limited social proof

- No educational content

## How To Find Leads
Compare several firms in the same niche and identify who appears weakest online.

## Outreach Example
“I compared a few firms in your category and noticed some positioning gaps that may be making it harder for buyers to see your difference.”

## Pro Tip
Competitor comparisons make your outreach more credible.

## Common Mistake
Using consumer marketing language with B2B businesses.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐⭐ Medium
- -

## 6. Angi

## Why This Works
Many local service providers depend heavily on lead marketplaces and have not developed a direct brand that attracts customers independently.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Electricians

- Plumbers

- Cleaners

- Remodelers

- Home improvement services

## What To Look For
- Few branded assets

- Weak reviews outside the platform

- No active social presence

- No direct lead capture system

## How To Find Leads
Search local providers and check whether they have any audience or trust assets outside the marketplace.

## Outreach Example
“You’re getting discovered through Angi, but there may be a real opportunity to build a stronger direct presence so customers come to you first.”

## Pro Tip
Talk about independence from platforms, not just more marketing.

## Common Mistake
Selling tactics instead of long-term control.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐ Easy
- -

## 7. Healthgrades

## Why This Works
Healthcare professionals care deeply about trust and reputation, but many profiles stop at basic directory visibility and never build educational authority.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Dentists

- Dermatologists

- Physiotherapists

- General practitioners

- Specialists

## What To Look For
- No educational content

- Weak review profile

- Outdated website

- No clear trust-building content on social media

## How To Find Leads
Find clinics with strong directory visibility but weak brand presence elsewhere.

## Outreach Example
“I noticed patients can find you through Healthgrades, but there may be a few missed opportunities to build trust before they book.”

## Pro Tip
Educational content often works better than promotional content in healthcare.

## Common Mistake
Using aggressive sales messaging with trust-based professions.

⭐⭐⭐ Medium
- -

## 8. TripAdvisor / OpenTable / Delivery Apps

## Why This Works
Restaurants and hospitality businesses already invest in customer acquisition, but many fail to turn reviews and traffic into stronger brand visibility.

## Who You’ll Find Here
- Cafes

- Restaurants

- Hotels

- Bakeries

- Hospitality brands

## What To Look For
- Weak Instagram presence

- Poor visual branding

- No short-form video content

- Strong reviews but weak owned channels

## How To Find Leads
Find businesses with excellent ratings but poor social presence or weak conversion pathways.

## Outreach Example
“Your customer reviews are strong, but your social presence does not fully reflect the experience people are already enjoying.”

## Pro Tip
Hospitality businesses care about bookings, foot traffic, and repeat visits, not just reach.

## Common Mistake
Talking about followers instead of customers.

## Difficulty Level
⭐⭐ Easy

## Category 2 - Social Media Platforms
- -

## 9. Instagram Hashtags

other_posts.title: 10 Quotes from Rich Dad Poor Dad
other_posts.text:
- -

🧠 10 Mindset Shifts from Rich Dad Poor Dad That Change Everything
- -

- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

Your mind decides if you stay stuck or get free. Most people never learn this in school.
“Never forget that fear and desire can lead you into life’s biggest trap if you are not aware of them controlling your thinking.”

Fear makes you say no to good opportunities. Desire makes you say yes to bad ones.
Tip: before any big decision, write down if you are acting from fear, from excitement, or from a clear plan. If it is fear or desire talking, wait 24 hours before deciding.
“Your mind is your greatest asset. It can also be your greatest liability.”

The same brain that builds a business can also talk you out of trying.
Tip: feed your mind daily with one piece of financial education, a podcast, a book chapter, or a video, instead of pure entertainment. What you feed grows.
“The poor and the middle class work for money. The rich have money work for them.”

Trading hours for a paycheck has a ceiling. Money working for you does not.
Tip: pick one small amount you can set aside monthly and put it into something that can grow or pay you back, even if it feels tiny at first.
“Assets put money in your pocket. Liabilities take money out of your pocket.”

This one sentence can fix most people’s finances.
Tip: list everything you own on paper. Next to each item write “pays me” or “costs me.” Be honest, this list will surprise you.
“The rich buy assets. The poor only have expenses. The middle class buy liabilities they think are assets.”

A car, a bigger house, or a new phone can feel like progress but often just drains cash.
Tip: before buying something big, ask “does this pay me back over time, or just cost me over time.” Then decide.
“A job is a short-term solution to a long-term problem.”

A job pays today’s bills but rarely builds lasting freedom on its own.
Tip: use your current job as fuel, not the finish line. Learn a skill or start a side project while you still have that steady paycheck.
“The rich don’t work for money. They make money work for them.”

This is the same idea repeated because it is the hardest habit to build.
Tip: every time you get paid, decide first how much goes toward something that can earn more money, then spend what is left.
“Schools teach you how to be a good employee.”

School teaches valuable skills but rarely teaches money management or investing.
Tip: treat financial education as a separate subject you study on your own, one article, one video, one lesson at a time.
“Wealth is how long you can survive without working.”

Real wealth is not your income, it is how many months you could go without a paycheck and still be fine.
Tip: calculate your number right now. Divide your savings by your monthly expenses. That is your current wealth score.
“Don’t work for money. Work to learn.”

Early in your career, chase skills and experience over salary. Skills compound, a single paycheck does not.
Tip: before taking or leaving a job, ask “what will I learn here” not just “what will I earn here.”

### 📌 PRO TIPS
- Read one finance book every two months, start with this one if you have not already

- Track every dollar for 30 days before trying to fix your budget

- Automate saving so it happens before you can spend it

- Surround yourself with people who talk about goals, not just gossip

- Review your asset and liability list every single month

### 💡 THE TRUTH
Nobody is coming to save your finances but you. Schools were built to create workers, not wealth builders, and most families pass down money habits, not money knowledge. The gap between rich and poor is rarely about intelligence, it is about financial education and which habits you were taught to normalize. The good news is this can be learned at any age, starting today, with zero excuses left once you know better.

### 🚀 QUICK START
- Write your full list of assets and liabilities tonight

- Pick one expense to cut this week and redirect it toward something that can grow

- Set a recurring day each month to review your numbers

- Find one book, channel, or creator to learn from consistently

- Tell one person your goal so you have accountability

### 🎯 BOTTOM LINE
Your mind is the real asset. Train it daily, feed it good information, and protect it from fear and desire clouding your decisions. Small consistent habits beat big one time efforts every single time.

🚀 CLAUDE CAN NOW BUILD YOUR ENTIRE YOUTUBE CHANNEL FROM SCRATCH
I used to spend weeks planning a channel before uploading a single video.
Now I paste 5 prompts into Claude and walk away with a full channel blueprint.
No guessing. No burnout. Just a system.
Here is the exact playbook 👇

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

- -

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1️⃣ FIND YOUR YOUTUBE NICHE
<role> Act as a YouTube strategist who identifies high RPM, low competition niches before they get crowded. </role>
<task> Analyze the top 10 YouTube niches right now and deliver a ranked breakdown for someone starting from zero. </task>
<steps>
- Identify 10 niches with strong RPM, low competition, and evergreen demand

- Per niche list average RPM range, content difficulty, and monetization paths beyond AdSense

- Assign a 3 word channel concept per niche

- Rank by opportunity score, weighing RPM against competition level </steps>

<rules>
- No saturated niches unless RPM clearly justifies the competition

- At least 2 non AdSense monetization paths per niche

- Ranking must be explicit, never “all are good options”

- Flag which niches are faceless friendly </rules>

<output> 10 Niches → RPM / Difficulty / Monetization / 3 Word Concept → Ranked by Opportunity → Faceless Flag </output>

Why it works: RPM data changes fast, and asking for a ranked list instead of a flat list forces the AI to actually compare tradeoffs instead of listing generic ideas you have seen a hundred times.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2️⃣ BUILD YOUR CHANNEL IDENTITY
<role> Act as a brand strategist who builds YouTube channel identities that stand out in crowded niches. </role>
<task> Create a complete channel identity that makes my channel immediately distinct from existing creators. </task>
<steps>
- Ask for my niche before starting

- Generate 5 channel name options that are memorable and brandable

- Write a tagline, one sentence that tells viewers exactly what they get

- Define a target audience persona with specific frustrations

- Build 4 distinct content pillars

- Identify my unique mechanism, the angle no existing creator owns </steps>

<rules>
- Unique mechanism must be defensible, not just a different tone

- Content pillars must not overlap

- Tagline must pass the “so what” test

- Persona frustrations must be specific, not generic like “wants to learn” </rules>

<output> 5 Names → Tagline → Audience Persona → 4 Pillars → Unique Mechanism </output>

Why it works: Most people skip identity and jump straight to filming, then wonder why nobody remembers their channel. Forcing a “so what” test on the tagline kills weak positioning before it wastes months of content.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3️⃣ 90 DAY CONTENT ROADMAP
<role> Act as a YouTube content strategist who builds 90 day roadmaps that compound authority over time. </role>
<task> Build a 90 day content calendar balancing SEO growth and viral potential for a new channel. </task>
<steps>
- Ask for my niche before starting

- Generate 12 video titles optimized for search, using keywords real viewers actually type

- Assign a sustainable upload schedule

- Label each video as SEO priority or virality priority

- Map content progression, showing how each video builds authority on the last </steps>

<rules>
- SEO titles must include a keyword viewers actually search, not a guessed keyword

- Virality videos need a hook concept, not just a clickbait title

- Progression must show clear authority building, not random topics

- Titles must stay under 60 characters where possible </rules>

<output> 12 Titles → Upload Schedule → SEO vs Virality Labels → Authority Progression </output>

Why it works: The label system forces balance so you are not chasing viral hits every video and burning out, while the authority progression step stops your channel from feeling like a random topic dump.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4️⃣ WRITE A FULL VIDEO SCRIPT
<role> Act as a YouTube scriptwriter who writes scripts that hold attention from the first second to the last. </role>
<task> Write a complete video script that stops the scroll and drives watch time. </task>
<steps>
- Ask for my video title and target audience before starting

- Write a hook, first 30 seconds with an open loop

- Agitate the problem, make the viewer feel the pain personally

- Walk through the solution, specific and actionable, no vague advice

- Deliver 3 key insights worth remembering

- Write one clear call to action and tease the next video </steps>

<rules>
- Hook must create an open loop in the first 10 seconds

- Call to action must be one action only, never three

- Problem agitation must feel personal, not generic

- No filler phrases like “in this video” or “without further ado” </rules>

<output> Hook → Problem → Solution → 3 Insights → CTA → Next Video Tease </output>

Why it works: Retention drops hardest in the first 10 seconds, so forcing an open loop there and banning filler phrases directly protects the metric YouTube’s algorithm rewards most.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5️⃣ SEO AND THUMBNAIL STRATEGY
<role> Act as a YouTube SEO specialist who optimizes every video element for discovery and click through rate. </role>
<task> Build the full SEO and thumbnail strategy for one video, covering title, description, tags, and thumbnails. </task>
<steps>
- Ask for my video topic and niche before starting

- Write an SEO optimized title, keyword first, under 60 characters

- Create 3 thumbnail concepts, each using a different emotional trigger and text overlay

- Write a full description with timestamps, keywords in the first 200 words, and one call to action

- Generate 8 tags mixing broad head terms with long tail variations

- Suggest A/B test variations for the strongest thumbnail </steps>

<rules>
- Title must be under 60 characters, no exceptions

- Each thumbnail concept uses a different emotional trigger

- Tags must include both head terms and long tail variations, no irrelevant tags

- Description opening 2 to 3 sentences must work as a standalone summary </rules>

<output> SEO Title → 3 Thumbnails → Description → 8 Tags → A/B Variations </output>

Why it works: Front loading the keyword in the title and description matches how YouTube’s 2026 algorithm weighs the first 40 to 60 characters and the first 200 words for search matching.
💡 PRO TIPS
- Run all 5 prompts in one conversation so Claude remembers your niche and stays consistent

- Save your favorite outputs as templates so you are not rewriting prompts every week

- Test 2 titles per video using YouTube’s built in experiment feature before locking one in

- Refresh old video descriptions every 90 days to keep search rankings fresh

- Never publish a script without reading the hook out loud first, if it sounds boring to you it will bore viewers too

📝 THE TRUTH
Nobody builds a successful channel from one lucky video.
It comes from a system you repeat until it gets boring.
Claude does not replace your creativity, it removes the blank page problem.
The niche research, the scripts, the SEO, all of it used to take hours.
Now it takes minutes, which means you can spend your energy on the parts AI cannot do, like your personality and your edit.
That is the real unlock here, not the AI itself, but the time it gives back to you.
⚡ QUICK START
- Copy prompt 1 and find your niche today

- Run prompt 2 right after to lock your channel identity

- Use prompt 3 to plan your first 90 days before you touch a camera

- Script your first video with prompt 4

- Finish with prompt 5 before you hit publish

🎯 BOTTOM LINE
This is not a shortcut to overnight fame, it is a shortcut to skipping the guesswork that stops most channels before they even start.

🤖 I gave Claude 7 tools and it started editing my videos for me.
No timeline. No dragging clips. No staring at software for hours.
I just drop the raw footage in, and it comes back looking like a real short form video.
Here is the exact setup:
- Speech to text: Whisper, MacWhisper, or SenseVoice Turns your raw talking into text so the AI knows what you said.

- Auto captions: Whisper generates SRT files, then ffmpeg burns them onto the video. No manual typing, no timing captions by hand.

- Auto cutting: Auto Editor Detects silence and dead air, then trims it out automatically.

- Text cards on screen: ImageMagick plus ffmpeg Drops in bold text overlays at the right moment, automatically.

- Voiceover: ElevenLabs If you don’t want to use your own voice, this clones a natural sounding one.

- Music and sound mixing: ffmpeg Balances music under your voice so nothing gets drowned out.

- B roll footage: Pexels API Pulls free stock clips that match your topic, no manual searching.

Once these 7 are set up, you just hand Claude the raw video.
It transcribes it, cuts it, captions it, adds music, and exports it in 9:16.
You still guide the creative direction. But the boring, repetitive part disappears.
⚡ PRO TIPS
- Always review the auto cut version before posting. AI sometimes trims a joke or key line by mistake.

- Feed Claude a style example (a caption style, a pacing style) so the output matches your brand, not a generic template.

- Run Whisper on the highest accuracy setting for niche topics with jargon, names, or numbers.

- Keep raw clips under 15 minutes per batch so processing stays fast and easy to fix.

- Save your Claude prompt as a template file so every new video takes one command, not a rebuild.

🔍 THE TRUTH
This is not “click one button and get a viral video.” You still need decent raw footage and a real hook idea.
What changes is the boring 70 percent: cutting silence, writing captions, syncing music, finding B roll. That part is now handled.
You are not replacing creativity. You are removing the manual labor around it.
Most people quit content because editing burns them out, not because they run out of ideas. This fixes that specific problem.
🚀 QUICK START
- Install Whisper (or MacWhisper for a simpler interface) and test it on one short clip.

- Install Auto Editor and run it on that same clip to see the silence removal in action.

- Set up ffmpeg once. It handles captions, music mixing, and text cards for every future video.

- Get a free Pexels API key so B roll pulls automatically instead of manual searching.

- Write one clear instruction for Claude describing your caption style, pacing, and tone.

- Test on one full video before batch processing your whole backlog.

📌 BOTTOM LINE
The tools are all free or low cost, and most already sit on your laptop. The real unlock is connecting them so Claude runs the full chain without you touching a timeline. Once it’s set up, editing becomes a five minute review instead of a five hour grind.

other_posts.title: 📚 20 BOOKS THAT WILL REWIRE HOW YOU THINK ABOUT MONEY (Save This Before It Disappears)
other_posts.text:
- -

Nobody taught us this in school. Not one class on how money actually works, how it moves, or why some people build wealth while others stay stuck in the same cycle forever.
These 20 books changed that for thousands of readers. Read in order.

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

🧠 PART 1: WHAT IS MONEY, REALLY?
- The Wealth of Nations | Adam Smith The OG economics book. Division of labor, trade, the “invisible hand.” Every other book on this list builds on ideas from here.

- The Economics of Money, Banking and Financial Markets | Frederic Mishkin Textbook but worth it. Learn how banks actually create money through lending. Once you get this, news about interest rates stops sounding like noise.

- Rich Dad Poor Dad | Robert Kiyosaki The classic starter book. Assets vs liabilities. “Make money work for you.” Simple but it plants a seed you’ll need later.

- The Richest Man in Babylon | George Clason Ancient parables, timeless lessons. “Pay yourself first” started here. Every money guru today is just repeating this book.

- Your Money or Your Life | Vicki Robin Reframes money as “life energy.” Once you calculate the real hourly cost of your job, you’ll never spend the same way again.

📈 PART 2: HOW MONEY MOVES (CYCLES, CRASHES, BIG PICTURE)
- This Time Is Different | Reinhart & Rogoff 800 years of financial crises. Same pattern every time. Debt builds up, everyone says “this time is different,” then it crashes anyway.

- The Changing World Order | Ray Dalio Bridgewater founder breaks down how empires rise and fall through debt cycles. Heavy but eye opening.

- Mastering the Market Cycle | Howard Marks Oaktree founder’s practical guide. “The most dangerous words in investing: this time it’s different.” Simple, sharp, no fluff.

- The Big Short | Michael Lewis Reads like a thriller but it’s the 2008 crash explained through real people who saw it coming. Painfully entertaining.

- Manias, Panics, and Crashes | Charles Kindleberger Every bubble follows the same script. Greed, mania, panic, crash. Understanding this pattern protects your money for life.

🧩 PART 3: WHY YOU KEEP LOSING MONEY (IT’S NOT MATH, IT’S YOU)
- The Psychology of Money | Morgan Housel 20 short stories proving wealth isn’t about being smart. It’s about behavior. This book alone will save you from dumb decisions.

- Thinking, Fast and Slow | Daniel Kahneman Nobel winner explains why your brain tricks you into bad money decisions. Loss aversion, bias, all of it explained here.

- Irrational Exuberance | Robert Shiller Why smart people make dumb bubbles together. Explains dot com crash, housing crash, and probably the next one too.

- Poor Economics | Banerjee & Duflo Nobel winning research that destroys the myth that poor people are just lazy. Understanding scarcity mindset changes how you see everyone, including yourself.

💰 PART 4: MAKING MONEY GROW (REAL STRATEGIES)
- Poor Charlie’s Almanack | Charlie Munger Multiple mental models, inverted thinking. “Tell me where I’m going to die so I don’t go there.” Practical wisdom disguised as a memoir.

- The Intelligent Investor | Benjamin Graham Buffett’s favorite book. Safety margins, market psychology, the roots of value investing. Dense but worth the slow read.

- A Random Walk Down Wall Street | Burton Malkiel The case for index funds explained simply. Most people trying to beat the market lose to people who just buy and hold.

- The Almanack of Naval Ravikant | Eric Jorgenson Wealth is not the same as money. Specific knowledge, leverage, and playing long games with long term people. Modern wealth building explained.

- Principles | Ray Dalio How to make decisions without ego getting in the way. Radical honesty applied to money, work, and life.

- The Black Swan | Nassim Taleb Rare events destroy fortunes. Learn to build a financial life that survives shocks instead of one that breaks from them.

✅ PRO TIPS
- Don’t read all 20 back to back. Pick 1 from each section first. That gives you a full mental map fast.

- Take notes by hand. Books about money hit different when you slow down enough to write the ideas out.

- Reread book 11 (Psychology of Money) every year. Your behavior changes as your income grows, and this book grows with you.

- Apply one idea per week. Reading without action is just entertainment.

- Skip books that don’t match your current stage. Beginners don’t need Dalio’s debt cycle theory yet. Start simple.

🔍 THE TRUTH
Nobody becomes wealthy by reading books. These books don’t hand you money. What they do is remove the fog. They teach you how money is created, how it moves, why markets crash, and why your own brain sabotages you.
Most people lose money not because they lack information but because they lack patience, discipline, and a clear framework. These 20 books together build that framework piece by piece. Economics gives you the foundation. Cycles give you timing awareness. Psychology explains your mistakes. Strategy gives you the tools.
Skip any one section and you’ll have blind spots. Skip psychology and you’ll keep repeating the same mistakes even with perfect knowledge. Skip cycles and you’ll get blindsided by crashes you could have seen coming.

🚀 QUICK START
- This week: read The Richest Man in Babylon (short, easy, high impact)

- This month: add Psychology of Money and Rich Dad Poor Dad

- This quarter: tackle one cycle book (Housel recommends Marks for beginners)

- This year: work through the investing section slowly, one book every two months

- Ongoing: reread your favorites yearly, your understanding deepens each time

🎯 BOTTOM LINE
Money is not magic and it’s not random. It follows patterns, cycles, and psychology that have repeated for centuries. These 20 books are not a quick fix. They are a long term education that pays off for the rest of your life.
Start small. Pick one book. Read it this week. That’s it.

Soft words open more doors.

Even small care has a big heart.

A clean space helps a calm mind.

Not every story needs your attention.

A small wait can make a big difference.

A few minutes of listening means a lot.

One small act makes the world better.

A calm breath can save a bad moment.

Kindness is easy to see.
12. Share more good energy online.
Not every post needs to be a fight.
13. Stay patient with people selling things.
A calm “no thank you” is enough.
14. Share your umbrella on a rainy day.
Small help feels big to others.
15. Keep your phone on silent in public.
Respect is a quiet kind of goodness.
16. Use less plastic when you can.
Small choices matter more than people think.
17. Smile at strangers.
Warmth spreads fast.
18. Praise people who are trying.
Good words can lift someone up.
19. Stop complaining and start solving.
Progress begins with a better response.
20. Forgive before you sleep.
Let today end softly.
🌟 Pro Tips
• Do one small good thing every day.
• Make kindness a habit, not a mood.
• Start with the easiest action first.
• Save this post so you can come back to it.
• Share it with someone who needs a gentle reminder.
