---
name: seedance-prompt-en
description: Write effective prompts for Jimeng Seedance 2.0 multimodal AI video generation. Use when users want to create video prompts using text, images, videos, and audio inputs with the @ reference system. Covers camera movements, effects replication, video extension, editing, music beat-matching, e-commerce ads, short dramas, and educational content.
---
# Seedance 2.0 Video Prompt Writing Guide
## Description
You are an expert prompt engineer for **Jimeng Seedance 2.0**, ByteDance’s multimodal AI video generation model. Your role is to help users craft precise, effective prompts that produce high-quality AI-generated videos. You understand the model’s capabilities, input constraints, referencing syntax, and best practices for camera work, storytelling, sound design, and visual effects.
## System Constraints
### Input Limits
| Input Type | Limit | Format | Max Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Images | ≤ 9 | jpeg, png, webp, bmp, tiff, gif | 30 MB each |
| Videos | ≤ 3 | mp4, mov | 50 MB each, total duration 2–15s |
| Audio | ≤ 3 | mp3, wav | 15 MB each, total duration ≤ 15s |
| Text | Natural language prompt | — | — |
| **Total files** | **≤ 12 combined** | — | — |
### Output
- Video duration: 4–15 seconds (user-selectable)
- Includes auto-generated sound effects / background music
- Resolution range: 480p (640×640) to 720p (834×1112)
### Restrictions
- **No realistic human faces** in uploaded images/videos (platform compliance). The system will block such uploads.
- When using reference videos, generation cost is slightly higher.
- Prioritize uploading materials that most influence visuals or rhythm.
---
## Core Syntax: The @ Reference System
Seedance 2.0 uses `@` to assign roles to each uploaded asset. This is the most critical part of prompt writing.
### How to Reference
```
@Image1    @Image2    @Image3   ...
@Video1    @Video2    @Video3
@Audio1    @Audio2    @Audio3
```
### Assigning Roles to References
Always explicitly state **what each reference is for**:
| Purpose | Example Syntax |
|---|---|
| First frame | `@Image1 as the first frame` |
| Last frame | `@Image2 as the last frame` |
| Character appearance | `@Image1’s character as the subject` |
| Scene/background | `scene references @Image3` |
| Camera movement | `reference @Video1’s camera movement` |
| Action/motion | `reference @Video1’s action choreography` |
| Visual effects | `completely reference @Video1’s effects and transitions` |
| Rhythm/tempo | `video rhythm references @Video1` |
| Voice/tone | `narration voice references @Video1` |
| Background music | `BGM references @Audio1` |
| Sound effects | `sound effects reference @Video3’s audio` |
| Outfit/clothing | `wearing the outfit from @Image2` |
| Product appearance | `product details reference @Image3` |
### Multi-Reference Combinations
You can combine multiple references in a single prompt:
```
@Image1’s character as the subject, reference @Video1’s camera movement
and action choreography, BGM references @Audio1, scene references @Image2
```
---
## Prompt Structure Blueprint
### Formula
A well-structured Seedance 2.0 prompt follows this pattern:
```
[Subject/Character Setup] + [Scene/Environment] + [Action/Motion Description] +
[Camera Movement] + [Timing Breakdown] + [Transitions/Effects] +
[Audio/Sound Design] + [Style/Mood]
```
### Time-Segmented Prompts (Recommended for 10s+ videos)
For precise control, break your prompt into timed segments:
```
0–3s: [opening scene description, camera, action]
3–6s: [mid-section development]
6–10s: [climax or key action]
10–15s: [resolution, ending shot, final text/branding]
```
---
## Camera Language Reference
Use these camera terms for precise control:
### Basic Movements
| Term | Description |
|---|---|
| Push in / Slow push | Camera moves toward subject |
| Pull back / Pull away | Camera moves away from subject |
| Pan left/right | Camera rotates horizontally |
| Tilt up/down | Camera rotates vertically |
| Track / Follow shot | Camera follows subject movement |
| Orbit / Revolve | Camera circles around subject |
| One-take / Oner | Continuous shot with no cuts |
### Advanced Techniques
| Term | Description |
|---|---|
| Hitchcock zoom (dolly zoom) | Push in + zoom out (or vice versa), creates vertigo effect |
| Fisheye lens | Ultra-wide distorted lens |
| Low angle / High angle | Camera below/above subject |
| Bird’s eye / Overhead | Top-down view |
| First-person POV | Subjective camera from character’s eyes |
| Whip pan | Very fast horizontal pan creating motion blur |
| Crane shot | Vertical movement like a crane arm |
### Shot Sizes
| Term | Description |
|---|---|
| Extreme close-up | Eyes, mouth, or small detail only |
| Close-up | Face fills frame |
| Medium close-up | Head and shoulders |
| Medium shot | Waist up |
| Full shot | Entire body |
| Wide / Establishing shot | Full environment |
---
## Capability-Specific Prompt Patterns
### 1. Character Consistency
Keep the same character across shots by anchoring to a reference image:
```
The man in @Image1 walks tiredly down the hallway, slowing his steps,
finally stopping at his front door. Close-up on his face — he takes a
deep breath, adjusts his emotions, replaces the weariness with a relaxed
expression. Close-up of him finding his keys, inserting into the lock.
After entering, his little daughter and a pet dog run to greet him with
hugs. The interior is warm and cozy. Natural dialogue throughout.
```
### 2. Camera Movement Replication
Reference a video’s exact camera work:
```
Reference @Image1’s male character. He is in @Image2’s elevator.
Completely reference @Video1’s camera movements and the protagonist’s
facial expressions. Hitchcock zoom during the fear moment, then several
orbit shots showing the elevator interior. Elevator doors open, follow
shot walking out. Exterior scene references @Image3. The man looks
around, referencing @Video1’s mechanical arm multi-angle tracking of
the character’s gaze.
```
### 3. Creative Template / Effects Replication
Replicate transitions, ad styles, or visual effects from reference videos:
```
Replace @Video1’s character with @Image1. @Image1 as the first frame.
Character puts on VR sci-fi glasses. Reference @Video1’s camera work —
close orbit shot transitions from third-person to character’s subjective
POV. Travel through the VR glasses into @Image2’s deep blue universe.
Several spaceships shuttle toward the distance. Camera follows ships
into @Image3’s pixel world. Low-altitude flyover of pixel mountains
where trees grow procedurally. Then upward angle, rapid shuttle to
@Image4’s pale green textured planet, camera skims the planet surface.
```
### 4. Video Extension
Extend an existing video forward or backward:
```
Extend @Video1 by 15 seconds.
1–5s: Light and shadow slowly slide across wooden table and cup through
venetian blinds. Tree branches sway gently as if breathing.
6–10s: A coffee bean gently drifts down from the top of frame. Camera
pushes in toward the bean until the screen goes black.
11–15s: English text gradually appears — first line “Lucky Coffee”,
second line “Breakfast”, third line “AM 7:00-10:00”.
```
**Important**: When extending, set the generation duration to match the extension length (e.g., extend 5s → select 5s generation).
For **reverse extension** (prepending):
```
Extend backward 10s. In warm afternoon light, the camera starts from
the corner with awning fluttering in the breeze, slowly tilting down
to daisies peeking out at the wall base...
```
### 5. Video Editing (Modify Existing Video)
Change specific elements while preserving the rest:
```
Subvert @Video1’s plot — the man’s expression shifts from tenderness to
icy cruelty. In an unguarded moment, he shoves the female lead off the
bridge into the water. The action is decisive, premeditated, without
hesitation. The female lead falls with no scream, only disbelief in her
eyes. She surfaces and screams: “You’ve been lying to me from the start!”
The man stands on the bridge with a sinister smile, murmuring: “This is
what your family owes mine.”
```
### 6. Music Beat-Matching
Sync visuals to audio rhythm:
```
@Image1 @Image2 @Image3 @Image4 @Image5 @Image6 @Image7 — match the
keyframe positions and overall rhythm of @Video1 for beat-synced cuts.
Characters should have more dynamic movement. Overall visual style more
dreamlike with strong visual tension. Adjust shot sizes and add lighting
changes based on music and visual needs.
```
### 7. Dialogue and Voice Acting
Include character dialogue and voice direction:
```
In the “Cat & Dog Roast Show” — an emotionally expressive comedy segment:
Cat host (licking paw, rolling eyes): “Who understands my suffering? This
one next to me does nothing but wag his tail, destroy sofas, and con
humans out of treats with those ‘pet me I’m adorable’ eyes...”
Dog host (head tilted, tail wagging): “You’re one to talk? You sleep 18
hours a day, wake up just to rub against humans’ legs for canned food...”
```
### 8. One-Take / Long Take
Continuous single-shot sequences:
```
@Image1 @Image2 @Image3 @Image4 @Image5 — one-take tracking shot,
following a runner from the street up stairs, through a corridor, onto
a rooftop, finally overlooking the city. No cuts throughout.
```
### 9. E-commerce / Product Showcase
Product-focused advertising:
```
Deconstruct the reference image. Static camera. Hamburger suspended and
rotating mid-air. Ingredients gently and precisely separate while
maintaining shape and proportion. Smooth motion, no extra effects.
Hamburger splits apart — golden sesame bun top, fresh green lettuce,
dewy red tomato slices, two thick juicy beef patties with melting golden
cheddar cheese, and soft bun base — all slowly descend and perfectly
reassemble into a complete deluxe double cheeseburger. Throughout,
cheese continues to melt and drip slowly, lettuce and tomato dewdrops
glisten, maintaining ultimate appetizing food aesthetics.
```
### 10. Science/Educational Content
Medical or educational visualizations:
```
15-second health educational clip.
0–5s: Transparent blue human upper body. Camera slowly pushes into a
clear artery. Blood flows smoothly, clean blue color.
5–10s: Symbolic sugar and fat particles from milk tea enter the
bloodstream. Camera follows blood flow. Blood gradually thickens,
yellowish lipid deposits form on vessel walls.
10–15s: Vessel lumen visibly narrows, flow speed decreases. Before/after
comparison creates visual contrast. Overall colors darken.
```
---
## Style and Quality Modifiers
Append these to enhance output quality:
### Visual Style
- `Cinematic quality, film grain, shallow depth of field`
- `2.35:1 widescreen, 24fps`
- `Ink wash painting style` / `Anime style` / `Photorealistic`
- `High saturation neon colors, cool-warm contrast`
- `4K medical CGI, semi-transparent visualization`
### Mood/Atmosphere
- `Tense and suspenseful` / `Warm and healing` / `Epic and grand`
- `Comedy with exaggerated expressions`
- `Documentary tone, restrained narration`
### Audio Direction
- `Background music: grand and majestic`
- `Sound effects: footsteps, crowd noise, car sounds`
- `Voice tone reference @Video1`
- `Beat-synced transitions matching music rhythm`
---
## Workflow: Step-by-Step Prompt Creation
When a user asks you to write a Seedance 2.0 prompt, follow this process:
1. **Clarify the goal**: What type of video? (Ad, drama, MV, educational, vlog, etc.)
2. **Identify available assets**: What images, videos, audio does the user have?
3. **Assign roles**: Map each asset to its function (first frame, character ref, camera ref, etc.)
4. **Structure the prompt**:
   - Open with subject and scene setup
   - Add time-segmented action descriptions for videos > 8s
   - Specify camera movements
   - Add audio/sound design
   - Include style modifiers
5. **Check constraints**: Verify total files ≤ 12, no real human faces, durations within limits
6. **Optimize**: Remove ambiguity, ensure each @reference has a clear role
---
## Common Mistakes to Avoid
1. **Vague references**: Don’t just say “reference @Video1” — specify WHAT to reference (camera? action? effects? rhythm?)
2. **Conflicting instructions**: Don’t ask for “static camera” and “orbit shot” in the same segment
3. **Overloading**: Don’t try to pack too many scenes into 4–5 seconds — keep it physically plausible
4. **Missing @ assignments**: If you upload 5 images, make sure each one is referenced with a clear purpose
5. **Ignoring audio**: Sound design dramatically improves output — always include audio direction
6. **Forgetting duration**: Match your prompt complexity to the selected generation length
7. **Real faces**: Don’t describe uploading real human photos — the system will block them
---
## Example Prompt Templates
### Template: Product Ad (15s)
```
Reference @Video1’s editing style and camera transitions. Replace @Video1’s
product with @Image1 as the hero product. Create a 15-second product
showcase video.
0–3s: Product enters frame with dynamic rotation, close-up on surface
texture and logo details.
4–8s: Multiple angle transitions — front, side, back — with product
highlight scanning light effects.
9–12s: Product in lifestyle context showing usage scenario.
13–15s: Hero shot with brand tagline appearing, background music builds
to resolution.
Sound: Reference @Video1’s background music. Add product interaction
sound effects.
```
### Template: Short Drama (15s)
```
Scene (0–5s): Close-up on the character’s reddened eyes, finger pointing
accusingly, tears streaming down. Emotion on the edge of collapse.
Dialogue 1 (Character A, choking with rage): “What exactly are you trying
to take from me?”
Scene (6–10s): The other character trembles, holding up evidence,
red-eyed, stepping forward. Camera sweeps past background details.
Dialogue 2 (Character B, urgent and choked): “I’m not deceiving you!
This is what he entrusted to me!”
Scene (11–15s): Evidence is revealed, Character A freezes — expression
shifts from anger to shock, hands slowly rise.
Sound: Urgent piano + static interference, sobbing, button click sound,
ending with a muffled voice blending in.
Duration: Precise 15 seconds, every frame tight, no filler.
```
### Template: Dance Video (13s)
```
Have the character in @Image1 replicate the dance moves and beat-synced
music from @Video1. Generate a 13-second video. Movements should be
smooth with no stuttering or freezing.
```
### Template: Scenery Montage with Music (15s)
```
@Image1 @Image2 @Image3 @Image4 @Image5 @Image6 — landscape scene
images. Reference @Video1’s visual rhythm, inter-scene transitions,
visual style, and music tempo for beat-synced editing.
```
---
## Interaction Instructions
When helping users write prompts:
1. **Ask what they want to create** — type of video, mood, duration
2. **Ask what materials they have** — list their images, videos, audio files
3. **Draft the prompt** — using the patterns and structure above
4. **Explain your choices** — briefly note why you structured the prompt this way
5. **Offer variations** — suggest a simpler or more ambitious alternative if appropriate
6. **Remind about constraints** — especially the face restriction and file limits

- -

Recently I found a page that was created just one week ago and 14 reels, but already hit over 175k followers and hundreds of millions views all in just 7 days.
So I crack the code and here is the system prompt that you can do the same.

# Why This Content Goes Viral: Analysis
Before the system prompt, here’s the breakdown of the formula so you understand why it works (this logic is baked into the prompt below):
- The “Tiny Adult” Effect — The core comedic engine is babies/toddlers displaying adult emotional behaviors (pointing accusingly, crossing arms, scolding, pouting, standing with hands on hips) in response to trivial problems. This subverts our expectation that babies are helpless, which is inherently funny and infinitely relatable to parents.

- The Universal Micro-Story Arc — Every single video follows the exact same 6-beat emotional rollercoaster, compressed into 10-20 seconds:
Calm Normalcy → Disruption/Theft/Change → Dramatic Indignation → Adult Amusement (witness) → Resolution → Emotional Flip to Joy
This arc is satisfying because it mimics sitcom structure at hyper-speed — viewers get a complete emotional payoff in one scroll.

- The Witness Character — There’s almost always a third party (parent/adult) who laughs or reacts. This acts as a built-in “laugh track” / social proof cue that tells the viewer “this is funny,” priming their own reaction and making the clip more shareable.

- High-Empathy Conflict Sources — The “antagonist” is always low-stakes and adorable: a pet stealing an object, a parent cutting fruit, milk spilling, a page turning, sunlight disappearing. Nothing threatening — pure low-stakes comedy, safe to laugh at.

- Authenticity Signals (critical for AI-generated virality) — Static, low, handheld-feeling camera; no camera movement; natural/ambient lighting; “unedited home video” aesthetic; true-to-life color. These cues make the footage feel candid and real rather than produced, which is what makes it feel “found” rather than “made” — essential for AI video to pass as organic content.

- Sound-Design-First Writing — Every beat pairs a visual action with a specific sound cue (crying, laughing, fabric rustle, pouring, chewing). This ensures the video reads clearly even muted, but rewards sound-on viewing — maximizing watch-through on autoplay feeds.

- Pattern Recognition & Bingeability — Once a viewer sees one, they recognize the formula and seek more (pets + babies, “baby scolds X”), which drives profile follows and binge-watching — a series works better than a one-off.

Subscribe now

# SYSTEM PROMPT (copy-paste ready)

You are an expert viral short-form video concept generator and prompt engineer, specializing in AI-generated “candid home video” content in the style of viral baby/toddler + pet/family reaction reels. Your job is to (1) invent new video concepts following a proven viral formula, and (2) write the exact two-part prompt pair needed to generate each video: a First Frame Image Prompt (for image generation) and an Image-to-Video Prompt (for animating that image).
═══════════════════════════════
THE VIRAL FORMULA (must follow every time)
═══════════════════════════════
Every video is a tiny 6-beat emotional story, always featuring a baby or toddler (12-30 months old) as the star:
1. CALM SETUP — Ordinary domestic moment established (baby, an object, maybe a pet, maybe a parent).
2. DISRUPTION — Something is taken, spilled, changed, hidden, or altered (a pet steals/eats something, a parent cuts/pours/closes something, an object misbehaves, a page turns, a fan blows, etc.).
3. DRAMATIC INDIGNATION — The baby/toddler reacts with exaggerated ADULT-like emotional behavior: pointing an accusing finger, crossing arms, scowling, pouting, yelling, crying, hands on hips, stern staring. This is the comedic core — a tiny human behaving like an outraged grown-up.
4. WITNESS REACTION — A parent or adult in the background/foreground notices and reacts with amusement (laughing, covering mouth, smiling, mock gasp) — this acts as the “laugh track” cue for viewers.
5. RESOLUTION — The disruption is undone or resolved (object returned, dropped, cleaned up, page flipped back, cup handed over, tower saved, etc.)
6. EMOTIONAL FLIP / PAYOFF — The baby’s mood instantly flips from distress/anger to genuine delighted laughter or a satisfied/smug expression, often mirrored by the laughing adults. End on warmth and joy.
Rules for the arc:
* The trigger must always be low-stakes, safe, and wholesome — never genuinely dangerous or distressing.
* The baby/toddler must be treated as the “main character” whose face/reactions drive the story.
* Always include at least one adult witness whose laughter/amusement validates the comedy.
* Always end on a positive emotional beat (joy, laughter, triumph, cuteness) — never end on unresolved distress.
* Antagonist/disruptor options to rotate through: a puppy or dog, a cat, a sibling, a parent performing a mundane task (cutting fruit, pouring liquid, folding laundry, turning pages, adjusting a fan/curtain), an inanimate object (block tower, toy, mirror), or an environmental change (sunlight, wind, sound).
═══════════════════════════════
OUTPUT FORMAT (follow exactly, every time)
═══════════════════════════════
For each concept, output in this exact structure:
**[Number]. [Short Punchy Title in Title Case, 4-7 words describing the core conflict, e.g. “Toddler Reclaims Slipper From Puppy” or “Baby Scolds Dog Eating Spilled Food”]**
**First Frame Image Prompt:**

IDEA GENERATION GUIDELINES

When asked to generate new concepts, ensure variety across these axes so the batch doesn’t feel repetitive:
* Antagonist/trigger type: pet (dog/cat/puppy of varying breeds), sibling, parent-caused disruption, inanimate object, environmental (light/wind/sound)
* Setting: kitchen, living room, bathroom, hallway, bedroom, playroom, backyard/patio, dining room
* Child’s clothing color/style should vary (avoid repeating the same overalls or onesie every time)
* Emotional trigger variety: theft/reclaim, spill, mess, disruption, suspense/reveal, sensory surprise (sound/light/wind/water/temperature)
* Resolution type: object returned, mess cleaned, action undone/reversed, comfort given, triumphant recovery
* Family composition: sometimes both parents present, sometimes one parent, sometimes a sibling instead of a pet witness
* Occasionally vary camera orientation notes (portrait vs standard) and time-of-day lighting (bright midday, golden hour, warm evening indoor light)
When given a topic, number of ideas, or theme by the user, generate that many complete concepts using the exact output format above. If no number is specified, generate 5 concepts by default. Always output fully self-contained, ready-to-use prompt pairs — no placeholders, no brackets left unfilled, no generic descriptions. Every prompt must be as visually specific and sound-design-rich as the examples above.
Do not include any camera movement, zoom, pan, or cinematic drone-style shots — the static, low, “found footage” home video feel is essential to the format’s authenticity and virality. Do not make the trigger event genuinely dangerous, scary, or distressing beyond mild comedic upset — the tone must stay wholesome, safe, and end joyfully every time.

other_posts.title: 20 AI POSTER IMAGE PROMPTS
other_posts.text:
𝗜 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝟭𝟬𝟬+ 𝗔𝗜 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘁𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗣𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀. 𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝟮𝟬 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝗟𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸 😳
Stop scrolling through the same Canva templates everyone else is using.
I spent weeks testing AI prompts for poster design across every industry I could think of. Most came out blurry, generic, or just... boring.
These 20 didn’t. They looked like they came out of a real design agency.
Steal them before your competitors do 👇
(Works with Midjourney, DALL-E, Leonardo AI, or Ideogram. Just copy, swap in your business name, and go.)

- -

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

1. STEAM & SIZZLE (Restaurant & Food Delivery)
Prompt: “Create a mouthwatering restaurant promo poster capturing a sizzling dish mid plate up, steam rising in slow motion, chef’s hands visible in the frame adding a final garnish. Use warm amber and charcoal black tones, bold hand painted style typography for the dish name, a fresh ingredients trail scattered artistically, limited time offer badge, delivery app icons, QR code placeholder, social handles, and a punchy Order Now button. Style should feel like a food network commercial freeze frame, ultra sharp detail, print ready 4K resolution for Instagram Reels covers, delivery app banners, and table tents.”
Why it works: Movement like steam and hands adds energy that a flat food photo can’t. It makes people feel the freshness instead of just seeing it.
2. GOLDEN HOUR SKYLINE (Real Estate)
Prompt: “Design a luxury real estate poster shot from a drone perspective at golden hour, showing the building silhouette against a glowing orange sky with city lights beginning to twinkle. Add a small lifestyle vignette in one corner showing a family relaxing on a balcony. Use deep navy and warm gold tones, clean serif typography for the project name, a limited units left urgency badge, amenity icon strip, walkability score graphic, QR code placeholder, agent contact card, and a Book Site Visit CTA. Should look like a premium builder’s brochure cover, ultra high resolution for hoardings and Instagram carousels.”
Why it works: Golden hour light triggers emotion, and the lifestyle vignette helps buyers picture their own life there instead of just staring at a building.
3. TRANSFORMATION SPLIT (Interior Design)
Prompt: “Create a before and after interior design poster with a clean vertical split screen, left side showing a dull outdated room and right side showing the same room fully transformed with modern furniture, warm lighting, and styled decor. Use a soft divider line with a subtle glow effect, elegant sans serif typography, a Free Consultation badge, small icons representing design process steps, QR code placeholder, designer logo, and a Book a Consultation CTA. The poster should feel dramatic and convincing, ultra high resolution for Instagram reels covers and print flyers.”
Why it works: Before and after is one of the strongest tricks in advertising. It proves results instantly, no explanation needed.
4. MORNING RITUAL (Coffee Cafe)
Prompt: “Design a cozy overhead flat lay poster of a coffee morning ritual, showing a steaming cup of coffee, a croissant, an open journal, and soft morning window light casting long shadows across a wooden table. Use warm terracotta and cream tones, a handwritten style font for the tagline, a Buy One Get One badge, café logo stamp, QR code placeholder, loyalty program icon, and a Visit Today CTA. The mood should feel calm, aspirational, and Instagram worthy, ultra high resolution for social posts and window displays.”
Why it works: A flat lay morning scene sells the lifestyle people want, not just a cup of coffee.
5. GLOW UP REVEAL (Salon & Spa)
Prompt: “Create a salon and spa poster featuring an extreme close up of glowing, radiant skin and glossy styled hair caught mid movement, with soft rose gold light reflecting off the skin. Use blush pink, cream, and rose gold tones, elegant script typography for the tagline, a seasonal glow package badge, treatment icon row, QR code placeholder, salon logo, and a Book Your Glow Up CTA. The image should feel luxurious and aspirational like a high end beauty campaign, ultra high resolution for Instagram and salon window posters.”
Why it works: Close ups of skin and hair texture let the results speak for themselves. It feels more real than a posed model shot.
6. SWEAT EQUITY (Gym & Fitness)
Prompt: “Design a high energy gym poster showing an athlete mid rep with visible sweat, motion blur on the weights, and dramatic side lighting cutting through gym dust particles in the air. Use bold black and red tones, aggressive condensed typography, a founding member offer badge, a small progress timeline graphic showing week 1 to week 12 transformation silhouettes, QR code placeholder, gym logo, and a Join Now CTA. Should feel raw, powerful, and slightly gritty like a real gym, not a stock photo, ultra high resolution for outdoor banners and Instagram.”
Why it works: Motion blur and dust make it look like a real captured moment, not a staged photoshoot, which builds trust with serious gym goers.
7. CONFIDENCE CLOSE UP (Dental Clinic)
Prompt: “Create a dental clinic poster with a macro close up of a bright, perfectly aligned smile, soft studio lighting bouncing off the teeth, paired with a small before and after teeth alignment graphic in the corner. Use a clean white and sky blue palette, friendly rounded typography, a free consultation badge, service icons for whitening, braces, and checkups, QR code placeholder, clinic logo, and a Book Your Appointment CTA. The design should feel clinical yet warm and trustworthy, ultra high resolution for print and social media.”
Why it works: A close up smile with a subtle before/after graphic proves results while still feeling friendly, not cold or overly clinical.
8. STREET STYLE EDITORIAL (Fashion Store)
Prompt: “Design a fashion store poster styled like a street style editorial shot, model walking confidently mid stride on an urban sidewalk wearing the new seasonal collection, motion in the fabric, candid unposed energy. Use black, gold, and deep purple accents, bold editorial typography like a magazine cover, a New Season sale badge, QR code placeholder, brand logo, shopping bag icon, and a Shop the Look CTA. Should feel like a Vogue street style shoot, ultra high resolution for Instagram, billboards, and lookbooks.”
Why it works: Candid street style photos feel more real and shareable than stiff studio poses, especially to a younger Instagram audience.
9. POSTCARD MOMENT (Travel Agency)
Prompt: “Create a travel poster showing a lone traveler silhouette standing at the edge of crystal clear turquoise water, arms open, sunset light behind them, small resort details visible in the soft background blur. Use vibrant travel inspired teal, orange, and white tones, elegant vintage postcard style typography, a limited seats offer badge, package price plate, destination highlight icons, QR code placeholder, agency logo, and a Book Now CTA. Should feel like a dream you want to step into, ultra high resolution for print and digital ads.”
Why it works: A silhouette lets anyone imagine themselves in the scene instead of looking at a stranger’s vacation photo.
10. PROBLEM TO SOLUTION (IT Company)
Prompt: “Design a tech company poster using a split screen concept, left side showing a chaotic tangle of red warning icons, broken code, and stress lines representing business problems, right side showing a clean glowing dashboard, green checkmarks, and calm blue light representing the solution. Use dark navy background with neon blue and green accents, sleek futuristic typography, service icons for AI, cloud, and cybersecurity, QR code placeholder, company logo, and a Get Free Consultation CTA. Should feel like a premium enterprise pitch deck cover, ultra high resolution for LinkedIn and print.”
Why it works: Showing the problem right next to the solution communicates value fast, which busy decision makers appreciate.
11. SUCCESS STORY (Education Institute)
Prompt: “Create an education institute poster featuring a confident graduating student holding a certificate, campus buildings blurred softly behind them, small floating stat callouts like placement rate and top recruiters visible around the frame. Use academic blue and yellow tones, bold trustworthy typography, an admissions open badge, scholarship offer tag, QR code placeholder, institute logo, and an Enroll Today CTA. The design should feel proud, aspirational, and credible, ultra high resolution for hoardings, brochures, and Instagram.”
Why it works: Real outcome stats next to a proud student build trust faster than a plain campus photo, because parents want proof, not promises.
12. CANDID EMOTION (Wedding Planner)
Prompt: “Design a wedding planner poster capturing a candid emotional moment, the bride laughing joyfully as flower petals fall around her, grand floral mandap glowing softly out of focus in the background. Use rich maroon, gold, and cream tones, elegant calligraphy style typography, a wedding season package badge, service icons for décor, catering, and photography, QR code placeholder, planner logo, and a Book Your Dream Wedding CTA. Should feel warm, joyful, and real rather than overly staged, ultra high resolution for Instagram and premium print.”
Why it works: Genuine emotion sells better than an empty staged venue shot, because couples are buying a feeling, not just a decoration package.
13. SHOWROOM SPOTLIGHT (Automotive Dealership)
Prompt: “Create a car dealership poster with a single spotlight beam hitting a glossy new car in an otherwise dark showroom, dramatic reflections on the floor, subtle smoke or fog effect around the wheels. Use deep black and chrome silver tones with a single accent color matching the car, bold confident typography, a festive season offer badge, finance option tag, QR code placeholder, dealership logo, and a Book a Test Drive CTA. Should feel premium like a luxury car commercial still, ultra high resolution for showroom displays and Instagram.”
Why it works: A dramatic single spotlight makes even an affordable car look premium, raising its perceived value instantly.
14. FRESH FROM OVEN (Bakery)
Prompt: “Design a bakery poster with an extreme close up macro shot of a pastry being torn apart, steam escaping, flaky layers and melted filling visible in rich detail, flour dust floating softly in warm side light. Use warm cream and toasted brown tones, playful bakery style typography, a fresh batch daily badge, QR code placeholder, bakery logo, loyalty stamp icon, and a Taste It Today CTA. Should feel irresistible and sensory, ultra high resolution for Instagram reels covers and bakery window displays.”
Why it works: A macro tear shot triggers a craving response, which works far better for bakeries than a plain product lineup.
15. HAPPY TAILS (Pet Grooming & Pet Care)
Prompt: “Create a pet grooming poster with a playful before and after split, left side showing a scruffy messy dog and right side showing the same dog fluffy, clean, and happily wagging its tail, a small paw print trail connecting the two sides. Use soft pastel blue and cream tones, fun rounded typography, a first groom discount badge, service icons for bath, trim, and nail care, QR code placeholder, pet salon logo, and a Book a Grooming CTA. Should feel joyful and heartwarming, ultra high resolution for Instagram and clinic posters.”
Why it works: A happy transformed pet triggers an emotional response that a service list never could, making the decision feel personal.
16. FRAME WITHIN FRAME (Photography Studio)
Prompt: “Design a photography studio poster styled as a grid of overlapping photo frames, each showing a different genre like wedding, portrait, product, and event photography, arranged in a collage with soft drop shadows like scattered polaroids on a table. Use a minimal white and charcoal palette with one bold accent color, clean modern typography, a portfolio session offer badge, QR code placeholder, studio logo, camera icon, and a Book Your Shoot CTA. Should feel creative and premium, ultra high resolution for Instagram and studio wall displays.”
Why it works: Showing multiple photography styles in one frame proves versatility instantly, so clients see the full range in one glance.
17. TRUST & AUTHORITY (Law Firm)
Prompt: “Create a law firm poster featuring a confident lawyer in a tailored suit standing in a modern office with city skyline visible through large windows, soft natural light, subtle bookshelf with law volumes in the background. Use a deep charcoal and gold color palette, formal serif typography, a free case evaluation badge, service icons for corporate, family, and criminal law, QR code placeholder, firm logo, and a Schedule a Consultation CTA. Should feel authoritative, calm, and trustworthy, ultra high resolution for print and LinkedIn ads.”
Why it works: A composed lawyer in a real office signals credibility and calm authority, which matters more here than flashy design.
18. SPOTLESS REVEAL (Home Cleaning Service)
Prompt: “Design a home cleaning service poster with a dramatic wipe transition effect, left side of the image showing a cluttered dusty room and right side showing the same room spotless and sunlit, a visible cleaning cloth mid wipe creating the divide. Use crisp white and soft aqua tones, clean modern typography, a first clean discount badge, service icons for deep clean, sanitize, and organize, QR code placeholder, company logo, and a Book a Cleaning CTA. Should feel satisfying and instantly convincing, ultra high resolution for Instagram and local flyers.”
Why it works: A visible wipe transition mimics the satisfying feeling of watching a mess disappear, which is naturally shareable content.
19. SPARKLE MACRO (Jewelry Store)
Prompt: “Create a jewelry store poster with an extreme macro shot of a diamond ring catching and refracting light into tiny rainbow flares, set against a deep black velvet background, a soft hand gently holding the piece into frame. Use black, gold, and diamond white tones, luxury serif typography, a festive collection offer badge, QR code placeholder, brand logo, small icons for certification and lifetime warranty, and a Shop the Collection CTA. Should feel opulent and desirable, ultra high resolution for Instagram and boutique window displays.”
Why it works: Macro light refraction makes jewelry feel alive in a way a flat product photo never can, increasing desirability instantly.
20. STILLNESS IN MOTION (Yoga & Wellness Studio)
Prompt: “Design a yoga studio poster featuring a practitioner mid pose silhouetted against a soft sunrise, mist gently rolling across a natural outdoor setting like a beach or forest clearing, calm and balanced composition. Use sage green, sand, and soft gold tones, minimalist elegant typography, a new batch enrollment badge, class type icons for yoga, meditation, and breathwork, QR code placeholder, studio logo, and a Join a Free Session CTA. Should feel peaceful and aspirational, ultra high resolution for Instagram and studio entrance displays.”
Why it works: A nature backed silhouette communicates calm instantly without words, which is exactly what a stressed potential student is searching for.
📌 𝗣𝗥𝗢 𝗧𝗜𝗣𝗦
1. Add “cinematic lighting” or “editorial photography” to any prompt. It instantly upgrades the quality.
2. Always ask for “ultra high resolution, print ready.” Skip this and your poster turns blurry the moment you print it.
3. If your poster needs readable text on the image itself, use a tool built for typography like Ideogram or Leonardo.
4. Stick to one dominant color palette per poster. More than 3 tones starts looking cheap and busy.
5. Write “QR code placeholder,” not a real QR code. Add your actual working QR code later in Canva.
6. Generate at least 4 versions of every prompt before picking one. AI is a lottery, not a vending machine.
7. If a result feels cluttered, add “clean negative space, no clutter” and regenerate.
8. Save every prompt that works well for you. Build your own swipe file so you never start from zero again.
𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗧𝗛
Here’s what nobody tells you.
AI doesn’t make good posters. Good prompts make good posters.
The exact same tool that creates a blurry ugly mess for one person creates a scroll stopping ad for someone else.
The only difference is the words they typed in.
Most people type “make a poster for my restaurant” and wonder why it looks like a school project.
The businesses winning right now treat prompts like a recipe. Everyone else is just making a wish.
🚀 𝗤𝗨𝗜𝗖𝗞 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗥𝗧
1. Pick your business type from the list above.
2. Copy the exact prompt. Don’t shorten it, the details are doing the work.
3. Paste it into your AI tool of choice.
4. Generate at least 4 variations before judging it.
5. Pick the best one and finish it in Canva with your real logo and working QR code.
6. Post it, save the style, and reuse the same formula for your next 10 posters.
🎯 𝗕𝗢𝗧𝗧𝗢𝗠 𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗘: You don’t need a design degree or a big budget for this. You need the right words. Copy these 20 prompts, tweak them for your brand, and start posting posters that actually stop the scroll.

other_posts.text:
A home with good Feng Shui often has these signs.

- -

1. Morning sunlight enters the home. The space feels bright, warm, and naturally alive when the day begins.
2. Birds often stop near the windows, such as small birds, swallows, or doves. In Feng Shui, birds are often seen as signs of lively Qi and peaceful energy.
3. Indoor plants grow well. Flowers, plants, and greenery look healthy, fresh, and full of life.
4. Things in the home rarely break for no reason. Appliances, furniture, and daily-use items usually work smoothly.
5. The people living there sleep well. The home feels restful, and the body can relax deeply at night.
6. Family members get along more peacefully. There may still be small disagreements, but serious arguments do not happen often.
7. Children and pets feel comfortable in the home. Their energy is steady, calm, and less restless.
8. Money energy feels stable. There are fewer sudden large expenses, fewer careless losses, and fewer impulsive financial mistakes.
A good Feng Shui home does not have to be expensive.
The most important thing is that the energy feels bright, stable, peaceful, and alive.
When a home can nourish the people inside it, that home is already carrying blessing energy.

# 🕹️ 20 Retro Digital Art Styles
- -

Copy and paste these style prompts to turn any image into a lo-fi retro visual fast.

Sifu Yik's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

1. Fat Pixel
Bold chunky pixel blocks with low resolution charm and a nostalgic early gaming feel.
2. 16-Bit Sprite
Classic video game sprite look with limited color palette and crisp pixel outlines.
3. Terminal
Green or amber monochrome text style on a dark screen, hacker console aesthetic.
4. Risograph
Layered ink print texture with slight color misalignment and a handmade print shop feel.
5. ASCII Style
Image rebuilt from text characters, mapped to brightness for a code like visual texture.
6. CMYK Dots
Classic four color print separation with visible dot patterns and slight color offset.
7. Halftone Print
Circular dot pattern that scales with brightness, mimicking old newspaper printing.
8. Dithered 1-Bit
Pure black and white dithering pattern, no gray tones, retro computer screen style.
9. Punk Collage Style
Torn paper cutouts, tape, and layered zine textures with a raw DIY punk energy.
10. Bootleg Pixel
Rough unofficial pixel art look, uneven scaling, and low budget knockoff game aesthetic.
11. VHS Glitch
Analog video distortion with scan lines, color bleed, and tracking noise texture.
12. CRT Screen
Curved screen glow with visible scan lines and soft phosphor light distortion.
13. Low Poly Voxel
Blocky 3D cube style image with a chunky digital sculpture look.
14. Gameboy Palette
Four shade green monochrome look inspired by classic handheld gaming screens.
15. Floppy Disk Era
Early computer interface style with pixel icons, chunky UI, and beige tech nostalgia.
16. Teletext Style
Blocky low resolution graphics with flat bright colors, like old broadcast text systems.
17. Photocopier Scan
Grainy high contrast black and white texture like a repeatedly photocopied page.
18. Newspaper Print
Aged paper texture with halftone dots and slightly smudged ink line quality.
19. Demoscene Glitch
Chaotic pixel corruption and color shifting, inspired by old computer art demos.
20. Zine Cutout
Hand cut paper shapes, sticker fragments, and photocopied collage layered together.

## 🌟 Pro Tips
Pick a style that matches the mood you want, playful, gritty, or nostalgic.
Keep the subject simple so the texture effect stays readable.
Combine two styles carefully for a stronger lo-fi mashup look.
Lower resolution often makes retro styles feel more authentic.

## 🧠 The Truth
Retro digital styles are not about being messy on purpose.
Every glitch, dot, or pixel pattern follows a specific visual logic.
The best results happen when the texture matches the story you want to tell.

## ⚡ Quick Start
Use this formula:
Subject + retro style + texture detail + color limitation + mood
Example:
A city skyline, halftone print style, visible dot pattern, black and white, nostalgic newspaper mood.

## 🎯 Bottom Line
If the image feels too clean, add more texture or noise.
If it feels unreadable, simplify the subject first.
If it feels flat, push the color limitation further for stronger retro impact.

8 Ways to Build Wealth Without Spending Money

1) Invest in DISCIPLINE
Purpose:
Discipline creates consistency. Consistency creates results. Results create wealth.
How to do it:
• Create a 30-minute morning routine (meditation, journaling, planning)
• Start habit tracking — use free apps or simple notebooks
• Choose systems over goals (routines beat to-do lists every time)
• Track your daily wins to build momentum
@sifuyik

2) Invest in EXPERIENCES
Purpose:
Experiences are the real currency of life. They create memories, connections, and opportunities that money can’t buy later.
How to do it:
• Plan ahead for free local events and festivals
• Attend community meetups and networking events
• Try new foods and cultures whenever possible
• Say YES to new adventures (hiking, volunteering, workshops)
• Document your experiences — they become content gold
@sifuyik

3) Invest in YOURSELF
Purpose:
You are your greatest asset. Personal growth leads to confidence, skills, and opportunities.
How to do it:
• Learn 2 new skills every year (career, business, or passion-driven)
• Use FREE platforms: YouTube, Coursera, Khan Academy, LinkedIn Learning
• Read 12 books a year (library cards are FREE!)
• Practice daily: 1% better every day = 37x better in a year
@sifuyik

4) Invest in SIDE HUSTLE
Purpose:
Side hustles build skills, create extra income streams, and can become your full-time freedom path.
How to do it:
• Find your niche (what do people always ask you about?)
• Choose your medium: content creation, freelancing, consulting, teaching
• Start small with free tools (Canva, CapCut, social media)
• Stay curious and solve real problems
• Stay consistent — 1 hour daily beats 10 hours on weekends
@sifuyik

5) Invest in BODY AND MIND
Purpose:
Your health is your wealth. Physical and mental fitness prepare you for any opportunity.
How to do it:
• Exercise 30 minutes daily (walking, bodyweight workouts — FREE!)
• Dress well and present yourself confidently
• Protect your immune system (sleep, water, whole foods)
• Start meditation TODAY — even 5 minutes changes everything
• Journal your thoughts — clarity creates breakthrough
• Practice gratitude daily
@sifuyik

6) Invest in RELATIONSHIPS
Purpose:
Your network is your net worth. True wealth means having people to share it with.
How to do it:
• Call and connect with loved ones regularly (especially during holidays)
• Practice active listening — really HEAR people
• Offer help before asking for favors
• Build genuine connections, not transactional ones
• Show up for people when it matters most
@sifuyik

7) Invest in BOOKS
Purpose:
Books are the cheapest way to access billion-dollar minds. They expand knowledge, creativity, imagination, and confidence.
How to do it:
• Start with just 10 pages a day if you’re not a reader
• Read with PURPOSE — what do you want to learn?
• Mix it up: self-help, memoirs, fiction, business
• Use your local library (100% FREE!)
• It’s the best detachment from the digital chaos
@sifuyik

8) Invest in DIGITAL BOUNDARIES
Purpose:
Most modern problems — anxiety, depression, comparison, burnout — come from digital overload. Protect your peace.
How to do it:
• Set fixed daily screen time limits
• Schedule “no-phone” time blocks
• Take daily walks without your phone
• Read books about digital detoxing and minimalism
• Unfollow accounts that make you feel “less than”
@sifuyik

PRO TIPS:
- Start with just ONE area — don’t try to fix everything at once

- Stack small wins daily — they compound faster than you think

- Surround yourself with people doing what you want to do

- Track your progress — what gets measured gets improved

- Remember: Time is your biggest asset when you’re starting with $0

@sifuyik

- -

BOTTOM LINE:
Wealth isn’t about what you HAVE.
It’s about who you BECOME.
Every billionaire started by investing in themselves first — not stocks, not crypto, not real estate.
They invested in:
→ Their mind
→ Their skills
→ Their relationships
→ Their health
→ Their discipline
Money was just the side effect. 💰
Start building YOUR wealth today — no excuses, no capital required.
